class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "(Re)seed LeavePolicy rows for the standard SEBPO leave types."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run",
            action="store_true",
            help="Report what would change; don't write anything.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        dry = opts["dry_run"]

        # Build name → ShiftType lookup once (case-insensitive).
        by_name = {
            st.name.upper(): st
            for st in ShiftType.objects.filter(
                is_active=True, category=ShiftType.Category.LEAVE,
            )
        }

        created = updated = skipped = 0
        details: list[str] = []

        for entry in LEAVE_POLICIES:
            aliases = entry["aliases"]
            kwargs = entry["kwargs"]
            description = entry["description"]

            # First alias that resolves wins.
            shift_type = None
            for alias in aliases:
                shift_type = by_name.get(alias.upper())
                if shift_type:
                    break

            if shift_type is None:
                self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                    f"  skip   {aliases[0]:6s}  — no matching ShiftType "
                    f"(tried: {', '.join(aliases)})"
                ))
                skipped += 1
                continue

            existing = LeavePolicy.objects.filter(shift_type=shift_type).first()
            if existing:
                # Compare to detect a real diff.
                changed = any(
                    getattr(existing, k) != v for k, v in kwargs.items()
                )
                if changed:
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
                        f"  update {aliases[0]:6s}  → ShiftType {shift_type.name!r} (pk={shift_type.pk})"
                    ))
                    updated += 1
                else:
                    self.stdout.write(
                        f"  same   {aliases[0]:6s}  → ShiftType {shift_type.name!r} (pk={shift_type.pk})"
                    )
            else:
                self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
                    f"  create {aliases[0]:6s}  → ShiftType {shift_type.name!r} (pk={shift_type.pk})"
                ))
                created += 1

            if not dry:
                LeavePolicy.objects.update_or_create(
                    shift_type=shift_type,
                    defaults=kwargs,
                )
                # Keep ShiftType description in sync if it's blank.
                if not (shift_type.description or "").strip():
                    shift_type.description = description
                    shift_type.save(update_fields=["description"])

        self.stdout.write("")
        verb = "would" if dry else "did"
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f"Done. {verb} create {created}, update {updated}, skip {skipped}."
        ))
        if dry:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                "--dry-run: nothing written. Re-run without --dry-run to apply."
            ))


# ==========================================
# FILE: ./leave/management/commands/apply_year_end_rollover.py
# ==========================================
"""Year-end rollover: carry forward + encashment auto-create + 60-day freeze.

For each policy with carry_forward_pct > 0, walk every active employee and:

1. Take `carry_forward_pct × (opening + accrued + carried_forward − used)`
   from the prior year, capped at `max_carry_forward_days`. Push to next
   year's `LeaveBalance.carried_forward`.
2. If `freezes_entitlement_at_cap` is True and the new carried_forward
   has reached `max_carry_forward_days`, set `entitlement_frozen=True` on
   the new year's balance and emit a FROZEN transaction.
3. If `encash_carry_forward_excess` is True, any unused balance beyond
   what was carried forward auto-creates a PENDING `EncashmentRequest`.

Run after the close of the calendar year (e.g., Jan 1 of the new year).

Usage:
    python manage.py apply_year_end_rollover           # rolls last year into current year
    python manage.py apply_year_end_rollover --year 2026  # explicitly: 2026 → 2027
    python manage.py apply_year_end_rollover --dry-run
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django.db import transaction
from django.db.models import F

from accounts.models import CustomUser
from leave.models import (
    EncashmentRequest,
    LeaveBalance,
    LeaveBalanceTransaction,
    LeavePolicy,
)


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Apply year-end carry-forward + encashment + freeze."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--year",
            type=int,
            default=None,
            help="The year being closed out. Default: current year - 1.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run",
            action="store_true",
            help="Print what would happen without writing.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        closing_year = opts.get("year") or (date.today().year - 1)
        next_year = closing_year + 1
        dry = bool(opts.get("dry_run"))

        self.stdout.write(f"Rolling over {closing_year} → {next_year}")
        if dry:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING("DRY RUN — no writes"))

        policies = list(
            LeavePolicy.objects
            .filter(carry_forward_pct__gt=0)
            .select_related("shift_type")
        )
        if not policies:
            self.stdout.write("No policies with carry_forward_pct > 0. Nothing to do.")
            return

        users = CustomUser.objects.filter(is_active=True)
        total_carried = Decimal("0")
        total_encashed_requests = 0
        frozen_count = 0

        for user in users:
            for policy in policies:
                old = LeaveBalance.objects.filter(
                    employee=user, leave_policy=policy, year=closing_year,
                ).first()
                if old is None:
                    continue

                unused = old.opening + old.accrued + old.carried_forward - old.used - old.encashed
                if unused <= 0:
                    continue

                carry_raw = unused * policy.carry_forward_pct
                carry = carry_raw.quantize(Decimal("0.01"))
                if policy.max_carry_forward_days is not None:
                    cap = Decimal(policy.max_carry_forward_days)
                    carry = min(carry, cap)
                excess_for_encash = unused - carry

                self.stdout.write(
                    f"  {user.email} · {policy.shift_type.name}: "
                    f"unused={unused} carry={carry} excess={excess_for_encash}"
                )

                if dry:
                    continue

                with transaction.atomic():
                    new_bal, _ = LeaveBalance.objects.get_or_create(
                        employee=user, leave_policy=policy, year=next_year,
                    )

                    if carry > 0:
                        LeaveBalanceTransaction.objects.create(
                            balance=new_bal,
                            delta=carry,
                            reason=LeaveBalanceTransaction.Reason.CARRIED_FORWARD,
                            application=None,
                            created_by=None,
                            note=f"Carry-forward from {closing_year}",
                        )
                        new_bal.carried_forward = F("carried_forward") + carry
                        new_bal.save(update_fields=["carried_forward", "updated_at"])
                        new_bal.refresh_from_db()
                        total_carried += carry

                    if (policy.freezes_entitlement_at_cap
                        and policy.max_carry_forward_days is not None
                        and new_bal.carried_forward >= Decimal(policy.max_carry_forward_days)
                        and not new_bal.entitlement_frozen):
                        new_bal.entitlement_frozen = True
                        new_bal.save(update_fields=["entitlement_frozen", "updated_at"])
                        LeaveBalanceTransaction.objects.create(
                            balance=new_bal,
                            delta=Decimal("0"),
                            reason=LeaveBalanceTransaction.Reason.FROZEN,
                            application=None,
                            created_by=None,
                            note=(
                                f"Carry-forward reached "
                                f"{policy.max_carry_forward_days}-day cap. "
                                f"Future accrual frozen."
                            ),
                        )
                        frozen_count += 1
                        self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                            f"  ⚠ {user.email} · {policy.shift_type.name} frozen at cap"
                        ))

                    # Encashment
                    if policy.encash_carry_forward_excess and excess_for_encash > 0:
                        EncashmentRequest.objects.create(
                            employee=user,
                            leave_policy=policy,
                            year=closing_year,
                            days_requested=excess_for_encash,
                            status=EncashmentRequest.Status.PENDING,
                            note="Auto-created at year-end rollover",
                            added_by=None,
                            updated_by=None,
                        )
                        total_encashed_requests += 1

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f"Done. Carried {total_carried} day(s); "
            f"{total_encashed_requests} encashment request(s) created; "
            f"{frozen_count} balance(s) frozen at cap."
        ))

# FILE: ./roster/admin.py

from django.contrib import admin
from import_export import fields, resources
from import_export.admin import ImportExportModelAdmin
from import_export.widgets import ForeignKeyWidget

from roster.models import Holiday, Roster, Shift, ShiftAttribute, ShiftType


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Import-export resources
#
# All resources use natural keys (e.g., ShiftType.name) instead of the
# auto-incrementing PK for `import_id_fields`. PKs differ between local and
# prod, so matching by name lets a CSV exported on a dev box import cleanly
# into production. Audit fields (added_by/added_at/updated_by/updated_at)
# are excluded — they auto-fill on save.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class ShiftTypeResource(resources.ModelResource):
    class Meta:
        model = ShiftType
        import_id_fields = ("name",)
        fields = (
            "name", "description", "category", "is_working_shift",
            "shift_timezone", "shift_start_time", "shift_end_time",
            "color", "has_attribute", "is_active",
        )
        export_order = fields
        skip_unchanged = True
        report_skipped = True


class ShiftAttributeResource(resources.ModelResource):
    shift_type = fields.Field(
        column_name="shift_type",
        attribute="shift_type",
        widget=ForeignKeyWidget(ShiftType, field="name"),
    )

    class Meta:
        model = ShiftAttribute
        import_id_fields = ("shift_type", "name")
        fields = (
            "shift_type", "name", "start_time", "end_time", "description",
        )
        export_order = fields
        skip_unchanged = True
        report_skipped = True


class HolidayResource(resources.ModelResource):
    class Meta:
        model = Holiday
        import_id_fields = ("date",)
        fields = ("date", "name", "is_active")
        export_order = fields
        skip_unchanged = True
        report_skipped = True

    extra = 0

    list_filter = ("category", "is_active", "is_working_shift")
    search_fields = ("name", "description")
    inlines = [ShiftAttributeInline]

            obj.added_by = request.user
        obj.updated_by = request.user
        super().save_model(request, obj, form, change)

"""Access tests for roster views + Roster API tests for the TimeLy contract."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, time

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.contrib.auth.models import Group
from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
from django.urls import reverse
from rest_framework.test import APIClient

from accounts.models import Department, JobLocation, WorkLocation
from employees.models import JobInfo
from roster.models import Shift, ShiftAttribute, ShiftType


User = get_user_model()


def _ensure_groups():
    for name in (
        "User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership",
        "Line Managers", "Department Heads", "All Employees",
    ):
        Group.objects.get_or_create(name=name)


def _user(email, **extra):
    return User.objects.create_user(
        email=email, username=email, password="x",
        first_name=email.split("@")[0].title(), last_name="T",
        **extra,
    )


@override_settings(
    STORAGES={
        "default": {"BACKEND": "django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage"},
        "staticfiles": {"BACKEND": "django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage"},
    },
)
class RosterAccessTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _ensure_groups()
        cls.eng = Department.objects.create(name="Engineering")

        cls.plain = _user("plain@example.com")
        cls.manager = _user("mgr@example.com")
        cls.report = _user("rep@example.com")
        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.report, reports_to=cls.manager)

        cls.hr = _user("hr@example.com")
        cls.hr.groups.add(Group.objects.get(name="HR"))

        for attr in ("plain", "manager", "report", "hr"):
            setattr(cls, attr, User.objects.get(pk=getattr(cls, attr).pk))

    def test_plain_employee_cannot_access_roster_week(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.plain)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("roster_week"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 403)

    def test_report_with_no_downline_cannot_access_roster_week(self):
        """A user who reports to someone but has no reports of their own
        is still a 'plain employee' for roster purposes."""
        self.client.force_login(self.report)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("roster_week"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 403)

    def test_manager_with_reports_can_access_roster_week(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.manager)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("roster_week"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

    def test_hr_can_access_roster_week_without_reports(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.hr)
        resp = self.client.get(reverse("roster_week"))
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)

# TimeLy roster API tests

_TIMELY_TOKEN = "test-timely-token"


@override_settings(TIMELY_API_TOKEN=_TIMELY_TOKEN)
class TimelyRosterAPITests(TestCase):
    """Contract tests for /api/v1/roster/ and /api/v1/roster/<employee_id>/."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        # Locations
        mhk = JobLocation.objects.create(name="MHK", code="MHK", is_active=True)
        mbd = JobLocation.objects.create(name="MBD", code="MBD", is_active=True)
        wfo = WorkLocation.objects.create(name="Work from Office (WFO)", is_active=True)

        # Shift types: one WORK, one OFF, one LEAVE.
        cls.eve = ShiftType.objects.create(
            name="EVE", category=ShiftType.Category.WORK,
            shift_start_time=time(14, 0), shift_end_time=time(23, 0),
        )
        cls.eve_attr = ShiftAttribute.objects.create(
            shift_type=cls.eve, name="EVE 1-10",
            start_time=time(13, 0), end_time=time(22, 0),
        )
        cls.off = ShiftType.objects.create(name="OFF", category=ShiftType.Category.OFF)
        cls.al = ShiftType.objects.create(name="AL", category=ShiftType.Category.LEAVE)

        # Employees with employee_id set.
        cls.alice = User.objects.create_user(
            email="alice@example.com", username="alice@example.com",
            first_name="Alice", last_name="A", password="x",
            employee_id="917", job_location=mhk, work_location=wfo,
        )
        cls.bob = User.objects.create_user(
            email="bob@example.com", username="bob@example.com",
            first_name="Bob", last_name="B", password="x",
            employee_id="918", job_location=mbd, work_location=wfo,
        )
        # Employee with NO employee_id — must be filtered out.
        cls.carol = User.objects.create_user(
            email="carol@example.com", username="carol@example.com",
            first_name="Carol", last_name="C", password="x",
            employee_id=None,
        )
        # Inactive employee with an id — must also be filtered out.
        cls.dave = User.objects.create_user(
            email="dave@example.com", username="dave@example.com",
            first_name="Dave", last_name="D", password="x",
            employee_id="919", is_active=False,
        )

        # Shifts on the test day.
        cls.day = date(2026, 5, 6)  # Wednesday
        Shift.objects.create(
            employee=cls.alice, date=cls.day,
            shift_type=cls.eve, shift_attribute=cls.eve_attr,
        )
        Shift.objects.create(
            employee=cls.bob, date=cls.day, shift_type=cls.off,
        )
        Shift.objects.create(
            employee=cls.carol, date=cls.day, shift_type=cls.eve,
        )
        Shift.objects.create(
            employee=cls.dave, date=cls.day, shift_type=cls.eve,
        )
        # Alice has shifts on the surrounding days too — for range tests.
        Shift.objects.create(
            employee=cls.alice, date=date(2026, 5, 5),
            shift_type=cls.eve, shift_attribute=cls.eve_attr,
        )
        Shift.objects.create(
            employee=cls.alice, date=date(2026, 5, 9),
            shift_type=cls.al,
        )

    def setUp(self):
        self.api = APIClient()
        self.authed = APIClient(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f"Token {_TIMELY_TOKEN}")

    # ----- Auth -----

    def test_anonymous_request_is_401(self):
        resp = self.api.get("/api/v1/roster/?date=2026-05-06")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 401)

    def test_wrong_token_is_401(self):
        c = APIClient(HTTP_AUTHORIZATION="Token nope")
        resp = c.get("/api/v1/roster/?date=2026-05-06")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 401)

    # ----- Daily endpoint -----

    def test_daily_missing_date_is_400(self):
        resp = self.authed.get("/api/v1/roster/")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 400)
        self.assertIn("date", resp.json())

    def test_daily_bad_date_format_is_400(self):
        resp = self.authed.get("/api/v1/roster/?date=2026-13-99")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 400)

    def test_daily_returns_only_active_employees_with_employee_id(self):
        resp = self.authed.get("/api/v1/roster/?date=2026-05-06")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        payload = resp.json()
        ids = sorted(row["employee_id"] for row in payload)
        # Carol has employee_id=None and Dave is inactive — both filtered.
        self.assertEqual(ids, ["917", "918"])

    def test_daily_work_shift_field_correctness(self):
        resp = self.authed.get("/api/v1/roster/?date=2026-05-06")
        rows = {row["employee_id"]: row for row in resp.json()}
        alice = rows["917"]
        self.assertEqual(alice["working_day"], "2026-05-06")
        self.assertEqual(alice["name"], "Alice A")
        self.assertEqual(alice["shift_attribute"], "EVE 1-10")
        self.assertEqual(alice["shift_start_time"], "13:00")
        self.assertEqual(alice["shift_end_time"], "22:00")
        self.assertEqual(alice["office_location"], "MHK")
        self.assertEqual(alice["work_location"], "WFO")

    def test_daily_off_shift_falls_back_to_type_name_and_nulls_locations(self):
        resp = self.authed.get("/api/v1/roster/?date=2026-05-06")
        rows = {row["employee_id"]: row for row in resp.json()}
        bob = rows["918"]
        self.assertEqual(bob["shift_attribute"], "OFF")
        self.assertIsNone(bob["shift_start_time"])
        self.assertIsNone(bob["shift_end_time"])
        self.assertIsNone(bob["office_location"])
        self.assertIsNone(bob["work_location"])

    def test_daily_no_shifts_returns_empty_list(self):
        resp = self.authed.get("/api/v1/roster/?date=2026-05-07")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(resp.json(), [])

    # ----- Per-employee endpoint -----

    def test_employee_range_missing_dates_is_400(self):
        resp = self.authed.get("/api/v1/roster/917/")
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 400)
        body = resp.json()
        self.assertIn("start_date", body)
        self.assertIn("end_date", body)

    def test_employee_range_end_before_start_is_400(self):
        resp = self.authed.get(
            "/api/v1/roster/917/?start_date=2026-05-10&end_date=2026-05-05"
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 400)

    def test_employee_range_too_large_is_400(self):
        resp = self.authed.get(
            "/api/v1/roster/917/?start_date=2026-01-01&end_date=2026-06-01"
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 400)

    def test_employee_range_unknown_id_is_404(self):
        resp = self.authed.get(
            "/api/v1/roster/9999999/?start_date=2026-05-05&end_date=2026-05-09"
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404)

    def test_employee_range_happy_path_returns_only_that_employee(self):
        resp = self.authed.get(
            "/api/v1/roster/917/?start_date=2026-05-04&end_date=2026-05-10"
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        rows = resp.json()
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 3)
        self.assertEqual(
            [r["working_day"] for r in rows],
            ["2026-05-05", "2026-05-06", "2026-05-09"],
        )
        # Last row is the AL leave: shift_attribute falls back to "AL".
        self.assertEqual(rows[-1]["shift_attribute"], "AL")
        self.assertIsNone(rows[-1]["office_location"])

    def test_employee_range_inactive_user_is_404(self):
        # Dave has employee_id=919 but is_active=False — endpoint should not
        # leak his data.
        resp = self.authed.get(
            "/api/v1/roster/919/?start_date=2026-05-05&end_date=2026-05-09"
        )
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 404)

# FILE: ./roster/services.py
# ==========================================
"""Operational helpers for the roster module — pattern auto-creation and
shift pre-fill.

Permission helpers (visibility / edit gating) live in `accounts.permissions`;
this module only contains roster-domain business logic.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, timedelta

from roster.models import Roster, Shift, ShiftAttribute, ShiftType


# Default Mon–Fri assignment is the EVE shift, specifically the "EVE 1-10"
# attribute (13:00–22:00). Sat/Sun fall back to the OFF shift.
DEFAULT_WORK_SHIFT_NAME = "EVE"
DEFAULT_WORK_ATTRIBUTE_NAME = "EVE 1-10"
DEFAULT_OFF_SHIFT_NAME = "OFF"


# --- Default-pattern auto-generation --------------------------------------

def _default_work_shift():
    """Return (ShiftType, ShiftAttribute|None) for new-user weekdays.

    Tries the canonical (EVE / EVE 1-10) pair first. If EVE doesn't exist
    (legacy DB), falls back to the alphabetically-first active WORK shift
    with no attribute.
    """
    eve = (
        ShiftType.objects
        .filter(is_active=True, name__iexact=DEFAULT_WORK_SHIFT_NAME)
        .first()
    )
    if eve:
        attr = ShiftAttribute.objects.filter(
            shift_type=eve, name__iexact=DEFAULT_WORK_ATTRIBUTE_NAME,
        ).first()
        return eve, attr
    fallback = (
        ShiftType.objects
        .filter(is_active=True, category=ShiftType.Category.WORK)
        .order_by("name").first()
    )
    return fallback, None


def _default_off_shift():
    by_name = (
        ShiftType.objects
        .filter(is_active=True, name__iexact=DEFAULT_OFF_SHIFT_NAME)
        .first()
    )
    if by_name:
        return by_name
    return (
        ShiftType.objects
        .filter(is_active=True, category=ShiftType.Category.OFF)
        .order_by("name").first()
    )


def ensure_default_pattern(user) -> bool:
    """Create Mon-Fri=<work>, Sat/Sun=<off> if the user has NO Roster rows.

    Mon–Fri rows are assigned the EVE ShiftType + EVE 1-10 ShiftAttribute
    (13:00–22:00). Sat/Sun get OFF.

    Returns True if rows were created. Idempotent — once a pattern exists
    (even a single row), this helper is a no-op so line managers' partial
    customisations aren't stomped on.
    """
    if not user or not getattr(user, "pk", None):
        return False
    if Roster.objects.filter(employee_id=user.pk).exists():
        return False

    work, work_attr = _default_work_shift()
    off = _default_off_shift()
    rows = []
    for wd in range(7):                       # 0=Mon … 6=Sun (Orbis convention)
        is_weekend = wd in (5, 6)
        target = off if is_weekend else work
        if target is None:
            continue
        rows.append(Roster(
            employee_id=user.pk, weekday=wd,
            shift_type=target,
            shift_attribute=None if is_weekend else work_attr,
            added_by_id=user.pk, updated_by_id=user.pk,
        ))
    if not rows:
        return False
    Roster.objects.bulk_create(rows, ignore_conflicts=True)
    return True


# --- Prefill daily shifts from pattern -------------------------------------

def prefill_shifts_from_pattern(request_user, employees, date_from: date, date_to: date) -> int:
    """Materialise missing Shift rows for (employee, date) in the range.

    Contract: NEVER overwrites an existing Shift row — approved leaves,
    manual overrides, and bulk-imported rows are preserved. Both the
    (employee_id, date) membership check AND `ignore_conflicts=True` on
    bulk_create enforce this.

    Returns the number of rows created.
    """
    if date_from > date_to:
        return 0
    days = [date_from + timedelta(days=i) for i in range((date_to - date_from).days + 1)]
    emp_ids = [e.pk for e in employees]
    if not emp_ids:
        return 0

    existing = set(
        Shift.objects
        .filter(employee_id__in=emp_ids, date__gte=date_from, date__lte=date_to)
        .values_list("employee_id", "date")
    )

    pattern_rows = (
        Roster.objects
        .filter(employee_id__in=emp_ids)
        .select_related("shift_type", "shift_attribute", "job_location", "work_location")
    )
    patterns = {(p.employee_id, p.weekday): p for p in pattern_rows}

    to_create = []
    added_by_id = getattr(request_user, "pk", None) if request_user and request_user.is_authenticated else None
    for emp in employees:
        for d in days:
            if (emp.pk, d) in existing:
                continue
            pat = patterns.get((emp.pk, d.weekday()))
            if pat is None:
                continue
            to_create.append(Shift(
                employee_id=emp.pk, date=d,
                shift_type=pat.shift_type,
                shift_attribute=pat.shift_attribute,
                job_location_id=pat.job_location_id,
                work_location_id=pat.work_location_id,
                added_by_id=added_by_id, updated_by_id=added_by_id,
            ))
    if not to_create:
        return 0
    Shift.objects.bulk_create(to_create, ignore_conflicts=True)
    return len(to_create)

# FILE: ./roster/models.py
# ==========================================
"""Roster app — shift catalog + daily assignments + weekly pattern + holidays.

Unified cell model per docs/PLAN.md: one `ShiftType` table holds every value
that can appear in a roster cell, categorised as WORK / LEAVE / HOLIDAY / OFF.
The weekly grid renders `{{ cell.shift_type.name }}` with no branching.
"""

from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models
from django.utils import timezone


class _Auditable(models.Model):
    added_by = models.ForeignKey(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name="+",
    )
    added_at = models.DateTimeField(default=timezone.now)
    updated_by = models.ForeignKey(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name="+",
    )
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        abstract = True


class ShiftType(_Auditable):
    """Every value that can appear in a roster cell."""

    class Category(models.TextChoices):
        WORK = "WORK", "Working shift"
        LEAVE = "LEAVE", "Leave"
        HOLIDAY = "HOLIDAY", "Holiday"
        OFF = "OFF", "Weekly off"

    name = models.CharField(max_length=100, unique=True, help_text="e.g. Morning, Evening, Night, Casual Leave")
    description = models.CharField(max_length=255, blank=True)
    category = models.CharField(max_length=10, choices=Category.choices, default=Category.WORK)
    is_working_shift = models.BooleanField(
        default=True,
        help_text="Usually derived from category; kept for payroll filter compatibility.",
    )
    shift_timezone = models.CharField(max_length=64, blank=True)
    shift_start_time = models.TimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    shift_end_time = models.TimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    color = models.CharField(
        max_length=20, blank=True,
        help_text="Optional tailwind class or hex to colour-code the cell (e.g. brand-accent, #FFC638).",
    )
    has_attribute = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["category", "name"]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.name

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs):
        # Keep is_working_shift in sync with category — simpler for reports.
        self.is_working_shift = self.category == self.Category.WORK
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)


class ShiftAttribute(_Auditable):
    """A named time-variant of a ShiftType.

    Example: `Evening` ShiftType has attributes `1PM start` (13:00–22:00)
    and `2PM start` (14:00–23:00). The roster picks a specific attribute so
    the employee knows exactly when to show up.

    When the user assigns a ShiftAttribute, the parent ShiftType is inferred
    (see `Roster.save()` / `Shift.save()` below). ShiftType's own `has_attribute`
    flag is kept in sync by this model's save / delete overrides.
    """

    shift_type = models.ForeignKey(
        ShiftType, on_delete=models.CASCADE, null=True, blank=True,
        related_name="attributes",
    )
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    start_time = models.TimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    end_time = models.TimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    description = models.TextField(blank=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["shift_type", "start_time", "name"]
        unique_together = [("shift_type", "name")]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.name

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)
        # Keep the parent ShiftType's has_attribute flag in sync.
        if self.shift_type:
            self.shift_type.has_attribute = self.shift_type.attributes.exists()
            self.shift_type.save(update_fields=["has_attribute"])

    def delete(self, *args, **kwargs):
        parent = self.shift_type
        super().delete(*args, **kwargs)
        if parent:
            parent.has_attribute = parent.attributes.exists()
            parent.save(update_fields=["has_attribute"])


class _LocatedRosterCell(models.Model):
    """Mixin: per-cell job/work location with employee-default fallback.

    Both `Roster` (weekly pattern) and `Shift` (per-date concrete assignment)
    can override the employee's contractual `CustomUser.job_location` /
    `CustomUser.work_location` for a specific weekday or date — e.g., "Tue
    in MBD office, Fri WFH." Null on either field means *inherit from the
    employee's contract default*.
    """

    job_location = models.ForeignKey(
        "accounts.JobLocation", on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name="+",
        help_text="Office for this cell. Blank = inherit from employee profile.",
    )
    work_location = models.ForeignKey(
        "accounts.WorkLocation", on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name="+",
        help_text="Mode (WFO/WFH/Hybrid) for this cell. Blank = inherit.",
    )

    class Meta:
        abstract = True

    @property
    def location_badge(self) -> str:
        """Short label for the cell badge — 'MHK', 'MBD', 'RAOWA', 'WFH', etc.

        Falls back to the employee's contract location when the row hasn't
        explicitly overridden it. WFH wins over the office bucket so a remote
        day reads as 'WFH' regardless of which office the employee normally
        sits at.
        """
        wl = self.work_location or getattr(self.employee, "work_location", None)
        if wl:
            up = (wl.name or "").upper()
            if up.startswith("WORK FROM HOME") or up == "WFH":
                return "WFH"
            if "HYBRID" in up:
                return "HYB"
        jl = self.job_location or getattr(self.employee, "job_location", None)
        if jl:
            # Prefer the canonical bucket (MHK/MBD/RAOWA) over the raw name —
            # handles both seeded short codes and Azure-AD full-address rows.
            from accounts.locations import office_bucket
            bucket = office_bucket(jl)
            if bucket in ("MHK", "MBD", "RAOWA"):
                return bucket
            return (jl.code or jl.name)[:6]
        return ""


class Roster(_Auditable, _LocatedRosterCell):
    """Default weekly pattern for an employee.

    One row per (employee, weekday). Used as a fallback when no `Shift` row
    exists for a concrete (employee, date).
    """

    class Weekday(models.IntegerChoices):
        MONDAY = 0, "Monday"
        TUESDAY = 1, "Tuesday"
        WEDNESDAY = 2, "Wednesday"
        THURSDAY = 3, "Thursday"
        FRIDAY = 4, "Friday"
        SATURDAY = 5, "Saturday"
        SUNDAY = 6, "Sunday"

    employee = models.ForeignKey(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="roster_pattern",
    )
    weekday = models.IntegerField(choices=Weekday.choices)
    shift_type = models.ForeignKey(ShiftType, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="+")
    shift_attribute = models.ForeignKey(
        ShiftAttribute, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="+",
    )

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["employee", "weekday"]
        unique_together = [("employee", "weekday")]

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs):
        # If an attribute is set, its parent ShiftType always wins.
        if self.shift_attribute_id and self.shift_attribute.shift_type_id:
            self.shift_type = self.shift_attribute.shift_type
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        variant = f" / {self.shift_attribute}" if self.shift_attribute_id else ""
        return f"{self.employee} · {self.get_weekday_display()} → {self.shift_type}{variant}"


class Shift(_Auditable, _LocatedRosterCell):
    """Actual daily assignment for (employee, date).

    This is what the weekly grid UI and the Roster API surface. If a cell has
    no Shift row, the view falls back to the employee's Roster pattern, then
    shows empty.
    """

    employee = models.ForeignKey(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="shifts",
    )
    date = models.DateField()
    shift_type = models.ForeignKey(ShiftType, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="shifts")
    shift_attribute = models.ForeignKey(
        ShiftAttribute, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="+",
    )
    note = models.CharField(max_length=255, blank=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["date", "employee"]
        unique_together = [("employee", "date")]
        indexes = [
            models.Index(fields=["date"]),
            models.Index(fields=["employee", "date"]),
        ]

    def save(self, *args, **kwargs):
        if self.shift_attribute_id and self.shift_attribute.shift_type_id:
            self.shift_type = self.shift_attribute.shift_type
        super().save(*args, **kwargs)

    @property
    def display_times(self):
        """Return (start, end) tuple from the attribute if set, else the type."""
        if self.shift_attribute_id and self.shift_attribute.start_time:
            return self.shift_attribute.start_time, self.shift_attribute.end_time
        return self.shift_type.shift_start_time, self.shift_type.shift_end_time

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        variant = f" / {self.shift_attribute}" if self.shift_attribute_id else ""
        return f"{self.employee} · {self.date} → {self.shift_type}{variant}"


class Holiday(_Auditable):
    date = models.DateField(unique=True)
    name = models.CharField(max_length=150)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["date"]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.date} — {self.name}"

@receiver(user_logged_in)
def ensure_default_pattern_on_login(sender, user, request, **kwargs):
    """Every employee should have a default weekly pattern.

    On first login (or any login where they still have no pattern), create:
        Mon–Fri → default working shift (Morning if present)

# ==========================================
# FILE: ./roster/upload.py
# ==========================================
"""Roster bulk upload — wide-format parser, applier, and template builder.

Wide layout (one row per employee, two columns per date — see docs/PLAN
and the plan file for the locked schema):

    Row 1: Employee ID | Employee Name | <date1> |        | <date2> |        | ...
    Row 2:             |               | Location | Shift  | Location | Shift  | ...
    Row 3: <emp_id>    | <name>        | <loc>    | <shift>| ...

The parser is read-only; the applier writes Shift rows inside one
transaction.atomic() and only if parse_errors is empty (all-or-nothing).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Iterable

import openpyxl
from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
from openpyxl.worksheet.datavalidation import DataValidation

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.db import connection, transaction
from django.http import HttpResponse
from django.utils import timezone

from accounts.locations import LOCATION_DROPDOWN_VALUES, resolve_location_choice
from accounts.permissions import visible_employees
from roster.models import Holiday, Shift, ShiftAttribute, ShiftType


User = get_user_model()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

LOCATION_TOKENS = sorted(LOCATION_DROPDOWN_VALUES)   # ('MBD','MHK','RAOWA','WFH')


@dataclass
class ParsedRow:
    line_no: int
    col_letter: str
    employee: object                 # CustomUser
    employee_id: str
    date: date
    shift_type: ShiftType
    shift_attribute: ShiftAttribute | None
    job_location: object | None      # JobLocation
    work_location: object | None     # WorkLocation
    is_holiday: bool = False


@dataclass
class RowError:
    line_no: int
    col_letter: str | None
    raw: dict
    message: str


@dataclass
class ApplyReport:
    created: list[ParsedRow] = field(default_factory=list)
    updated: list[ParsedRow] = field(default_factory=list)
    skipped_scope: list[RowError] = field(default_factory=list)
    parse_errors: list[RowError] = field(default_factory=list)
    duplicates: list[RowError] = field(default_factory=list)
    applied: bool = False

    @property
    def has_errors(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.parse_errors or self.duplicates)

    @property
    def total_writes(self) -> int:
        return len(self.created) + len(self.updated)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shift-name + location + employee_id + date resolution
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _build_shift_cache() -> dict[str, tuple[ShiftType, ShiftAttribute | None]]:
    """Two queries: every active ShiftAttribute (with parent type) and every
    active ShiftType with `has_attribute=False`. Returns a dict keyed by
    lowercased name. Attribute names win over type names on collision (the
    same precedence as `_resolve_shift_name`).
    """
    cache: dict[str, tuple[ShiftType, ShiftAttribute | None]] = {}
    for attr in (
        ShiftAttribute.objects
        .filter(shift_type__is_active=True, shift_type__isnull=False)
        .select_related("shift_type")
    ):
        cache[attr.name.lower()] = (attr.shift_type, attr)
    for st in ShiftType.objects.filter(is_active=True, has_attribute=False):
        cache.setdefault(st.name.lower(), (st, None))
    return cache


def _resolve_shift_name(
    name: str,
    cache: dict[str, tuple[ShiftType, ShiftAttribute | None]],
) -> tuple[ShiftType, ShiftAttribute | None]:
    """Resolve a shift cell value from the cache built by ``_build_shift_cache``."""
    if name is None or not str(name).strip():
        raise ValueError("Empty shift value.")
    key = str(name).strip().lower()
    hit = cache.get(key)
    if hit is not None:
        return hit
    # Cache miss: distinguish "type exists but needs a variant" from
    # "unknown name" so the error message stays useful.
    st = ShiftType.objects.filter(name__iexact=name, is_active=True).first()
    if st is not None and st.has_attribute:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Shift '{name}' requires a specific attribute (e.g. variant). "
            f"Pick one of its attribute names."
        )
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown shift name: '{str(name).strip()}'.")


def _build_location_cache() -> dict[str, tuple]:
    """Resolve every canonical dropdown token once (4 calls, ~6 queries total)
    and cache the FK pair. Saves ~3 queries per Shift cell on big uploads.
    """
    return {
        token.upper(): resolve_location_choice(token)
        for token in LOCATION_DROPDOWN_VALUES
    }


def _resolve_location_token(token: str | None, cache: dict[str, tuple]):
    """Empty token → (None, None). Valid token → cached FKs. Else ValueError."""
    if token is None:
        return None, None
    raw = str(token).strip()
    if not raw:
        return None, None
    upper = raw.upper()
    hit = cache.get(upper)
    if hit is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown location '{raw}'. Expected one of {sorted(LOCATION_DROPDOWN_VALUES)}."
        )
    return hit


# Backwards-compatible wrappers — the bare helpers still work for the unit
# tests and any single-call path. They build a tiny cache on demand.
def _resolve_shift(name: str) -> tuple[ShiftType, ShiftAttribute | None]:
    return _resolve_shift_name(name, _build_shift_cache())


def _resolve_location(token: str | None):
    return _resolve_location_token(token, _build_location_cache())


def _coerce_employee_id(value) -> str:
    """xlsx may hand us int/float for numeric employee_id cells. CSV gives str.
    Normalise to a clean string suitable for `CustomUser.employee_id` lookup.
    """
    if value is None:
        raise ValueError("Empty employee_id.")
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        raise ValueError(f"Bad employee_id: {value!r}.")
    if isinstance(value, int):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, float):
        if not value.is_integer():
            raise ValueError(
                f"Employee_id '{value}' looks like a decimal — expected an integer or text."
            )
        return str(int(value))
    s = str(value).strip()
    if not s:
        raise ValueError("Empty employee_id.")
    return s


def _parse_cell_date(raw, today: date) -> date:
    """Accept either a native datetime.date (xlsx native date cell) or an
    ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. Reject anything else and dates more than 365
    days from today.
    """
    if raw is None:
        raise ValueError("Empty date.")
    if isinstance(raw, datetime):
        parsed = raw.date()
    elif isinstance(raw, date):
        parsed = raw
    else:
        s = str(raw).strip()
        if not s:
            raise ValueError("Empty date.")
        try:
            parsed = datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d").date()
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(f"Bad date '{s}' — use YYYY-MM-DD.")
    if abs((parsed - today).days) > 365:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Date {parsed.isoformat()} is more than a year from today — likely a typo."
        )
    return parsed


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File reading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _read_xlsx_rows(file_obj) -> list[list]:
    """Return the first worksheet as a list of rows; each row a list of cells.
    Cell values are kept native (datetime.date stays a date, int stays int)."""
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(file_obj, data_only=True, read_only=True)
    ws = wb.worksheets[0]
    rows = []
    for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True):
        rows.append(list(row))
    return rows


def _read_csv_rows(file_obj) -> list[list]:
    """Decode and read CSV. Tolerate UTF-8 BOM."""
    raw = file_obj.read()
    if isinstance(raw, bytes):
        text = raw.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace")
    else:
        text = raw
    reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(text))
    return [list(row) for row in reader]


def _load_rows(file_obj, filename: str) -> list[list]:
    name = (filename or "").lower()
    if name.endswith(".xlsx"):
        return _read_xlsx_rows(file_obj)
    if name.endswith(".csv"):
        return _read_csv_rows(file_obj)
    raise ValueError(
        f"Unsupported file type: {filename!r}. Upload an .xlsx or .csv file."
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Header discovery
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _discover_date_columns(
    header_row: list,
    sub_header_row: list,
    today: date,
) -> list[tuple[date, int, int]]:
    """Walk header_row from index 2 (column C) onward. Every non-empty cell
    marks a date column whose right-hand neighbour is the Shift column.

    Returns a list of (date, location_col_idx, shift_col_idx) tuples.

    Raises ValueError with a header-level message if the structure is wrong:
    sub-headers must read 'Location' / 'Shift' under each date.
    """
    cols: list[tuple[date, int, int]] = []
    for idx in range(2, len(header_row)):
        cell = header_row[idx]
        if cell is None or (isinstance(cell, str) and not cell.strip()):
            continue
        try:
            d = _parse_cell_date(cell, today)
        except ValueError as exc:
            col_letter = get_column_letter(idx + 1)
            raise ValueError(f"Header column {col_letter}: {exc}")
        shift_idx = idx + 1
        loc_label = _norm(sub_header_row[idx] if idx < len(sub_header_row) else None)
        shift_label = _norm(sub_header_row[shift_idx] if shift_idx < len(sub_header_row) else None)
        col_letter = get_column_letter(idx + 1)
        if loc_label != "location":
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sub-header under {col_letter} should be 'Location' (found {loc_label!r})."
            )
        if shift_label != "shift":
            shift_col = get_column_letter(shift_idx + 1)
            raise ValueError(
                f"Sub-header under {shift_col} should be 'Shift' (found {shift_label!r})."
            )
        cols.append((d, idx, shift_idx))
    if not cols:
        raise ValueError(
            "No date columns found. Row 1 should list dates from column C onwards "
            "with 'Location' and 'Shift' as sub-headers in row 2."
        )
    return cols


def _norm(value) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return ""
    return str(value).strip().lower()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parser
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_upload(
    file_obj,
    filename: str,
    *,
    today: date,
) -> tuple[list[ParsedRow], list[RowError], list[RowError]]:
    """Read the uploaded file and produce ParsedRow / RowError lists.

    Returns (parsed_rows, parse_errors, duplicate_errors). Read-only —
    no DB writes.

    Lookups (employee, shift, location, holiday) are built once up-front so
    parsing a 700-employee × 7-day file stays around ~6 queries total instead
    of ~25,000.
    """
    rows = _load_rows(file_obj, filename)
    parse_errors: list[RowError] = []
    dup_errors: list[RowError] = []
    parsed: list[ParsedRow] = []
    seen: dict[tuple[str, date], int] = {}     # (emp_id_str, date) → line_no of first sighting

    if len(rows) < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "File is empty or has only one row. Expected at least: date headers, "
            "Location/Shift sub-headers, and one employee row."
        )

    header_row = rows[0]
    sub_header_row = rows[1] if len(rows) > 1 else []
    date_cols = _discover_date_columns(header_row, sub_header_row, today)

    # --- Build lookup caches (5 queries total, regardless of file size) ---

    # 1. Tag holidays.
    all_dates = {d for d, _, _ in date_cols}
    holiday_dates = set(
        Holiday.objects.filter(date__in=all_dates, is_active=True)
                       .values_list("date", flat=True)
    )

    # 2. Pre-scan employee_id cells (best-effort — invalid values are silently
    #    skipped here and re-raised inside the main loop for error reporting).
    candidate_ids: set[str] = set()
    for raw_row in rows[2:]:
        if not raw_row:
            continue
        try:
            candidate_ids.add(_coerce_employee_id(raw_row[0]))
        except ValueError:
            pass

    # 3. One query for all employees referenced in the file.
    if candidate_ids:
        emp_cache = {
            u.employee_id: u
            for u in User.objects
                         .filter(is_active=True, employee_id__in=candidate_ids)
        }
    else:
        emp_cache = {}

    # 4. Shift names and location tokens.
    shift_cache = _build_shift_cache()
    location_cache = _build_location_cache()

    # --- Main loop: dict lookups only, zero queries per cell ---

    for line_no_zero, raw_row in enumerate(rows[2:], start=3):
        # line_no_zero is the 1-based file line (header rows are lines 1 and 2).
        emp_id_cell = raw_row[0] if len(raw_row) > 0 else None
        name_cell = raw_row[1] if len(raw_row) > 1 else None
        # Skip wholly-empty rows silently.
        if _is_blank(emp_id_cell) and all(_is_blank(raw_row[c]) for d, c, _ in date_cols if c < len(raw_row)):
            continue

        # Coerce + look up the employee.
        try:
            emp_id_str = _coerce_employee_id(emp_id_cell)
        except ValueError as exc:
            parse_errors.append(RowError(
                line_no=line_no_zero, col_letter="A",
                raw={"Employee ID": _safe_str(emp_id_cell), "Employee Name": _safe_str(name_cell)},
                message=str(exc),
            ))
            continue

        employee = emp_cache.get(emp_id_str)
        if employee is None:
            parse_errors.append(RowError(
                line_no=line_no_zero, col_letter="A",
                raw={"Employee ID": emp_id_str, "Employee Name": _safe_str(name_cell)},
                message=f"No active employee with employee_id '{emp_id_str}'.",
            ))
            continue

        for d, loc_idx, shift_idx in date_cols:
            loc_cell = raw_row[loc_idx] if loc_idx < len(raw_row) else None
            shift_cell = raw_row[shift_idx] if shift_idx < len(raw_row) else None

            loc_blank = _is_blank(loc_cell)
            shift_blank = _is_blank(shift_cell)

            if loc_blank and shift_blank:
                # Manager left this (employee, date) untouched.
                continue

            shift_col_letter = get_column_letter(shift_idx + 1)
            raw_snapshot = {
                "Employee ID": emp_id_str,
                "Employee Name": _safe_str(name_cell),
                "Date": d.isoformat(),
                "Location": _safe_str(loc_cell),
                "Shift": _safe_str(shift_cell),
            }

            if shift_blank:
                parse_errors.append(RowError(
                    line_no=line_no_zero, col_letter=shift_col_letter,
                    raw=raw_snapshot,
                    message=f"Location filled but Shift is empty on {d.isoformat()}.",
                ))
                continue

            # Resolve shift name (dict lookup).
            try:
                shift_type, shift_attr = _resolve_shift_name(shift_cell, shift_cache)
            except ValueError as exc:
                parse_errors.append(RowError(
                    line_no=line_no_zero, col_letter=shift_col_letter,
                    raw=raw_snapshot, message=str(exc),
                ))
                continue

            # Resolve location (dict lookup).
            try:
                jl, wl = _resolve_location_token(loc_cell, location_cache)
            except ValueError as exc:
                loc_col_letter = get_column_letter(loc_idx + 1)
                parse_errors.append(RowError(
                    line_no=line_no_zero, col_letter=loc_col_letter,
                    raw=raw_snapshot, message=str(exc),
                ))
                continue

            # Duplicate (employee, date) within file?
            key = (emp_id_str, d)
            if key in seen:
                dup_errors.append(RowError(
                    line_no=line_no_zero, col_letter=shift_col_letter,
                    raw=raw_snapshot,
                    message=(
                        f"Duplicate of row {seen[key]} — same employee_id {emp_id_str} "
                        f"and date {d.isoformat()} appears twice."
                    ),
                ))
                continue
            seen[key] = line_no_zero

            parsed.append(ParsedRow(
                line_no=line_no_zero, col_letter=shift_col_letter,
                employee=employee, employee_id=emp_id_str, date=d,
                shift_type=shift_type, shift_attribute=shift_attr,
                job_location=jl, work_location=wl,
                is_holiday=(d in holiday_dates),
            ))

    return parsed, parse_errors, dup_errors


def _is_blank(value) -> bool:
    if value is None:
        return True
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return value.strip() == ""
    return False


def _safe_str(value) -> str:
    if value is None:
        return ""
    return str(value)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Applier
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def apply_upload(
    viewer,
    parsed_rows: list[ParsedRow],
    viewer_visible_pks: set,
) -> ApplyReport:
    """Apply parsed rows to the Shift table inside one transaction.

    Rows whose employee is outside `viewer_visible_pks` are not written; they
    appear in `report.skipped_scope` instead.

    Implementation: one pre-query to learn which (employee, date) pairs already
    exist, then a single ``bulk_create(update_conflicts=True)`` to insert new
    rows and overwrite existing ones in one round-trip. The 700-employee × 7-day
    case settles in ~3 queries total instead of ~10,000.

    Safety: ``bulk_create`` bypasses ``Model.save()``, so the parent-type sync
    that ``Shift.save()`` does (line 228) is skipped. That's fine because
    ``parse_upload`` already populates ``row.shift_type`` from the attribute's
    parent — the invariant is maintained at the source.
    """
    report = ApplyReport()

    in_scope: list[ParsedRow] = []
    for row in parsed_rows:
        if row.employee.pk in viewer_visible_pks:
            in_scope.append(row)
        else:
            report.skipped_scope.append(RowError(
                line_no=row.line_no, col_letter="A",
                raw={
                    "Employee ID": row.employee_id,
                    "Date": row.date.isoformat(),
                    "Shift": row.shift_type.name,
                },
                message="Outside your managed scope.",
            ))

    if not in_scope:
        report.applied = True   # nothing to do, but the upload itself didn't error
        return report

    # Find which (employee, date) pairs already exist so we can report the
    # create-vs-update split. One query for the whole batch.
    emp_pks = {r.employee.pk for r in in_scope}
    dates = {r.date for r in in_scope}
    existing_pairs = set(
        Shift.objects
        .filter(employee_id__in=emp_pks, date__in=dates)
        .values_list("employee_id", "date")
    )

    now = timezone.now()
    objs: list[Shift] = []
    for r in in_scope:
        objs.append(Shift(
            employee=r.employee, date=r.date,
            shift_type=r.shift_type,
            shift_attribute=r.shift_attribute,
            job_location=r.job_location,
            work_location=r.work_location,
            # added_* are only written on INSERT (not in update_fields) so
            # they stay untouched when an existing row is overwritten.
            added_by=viewer, added_at=now,
            updated_by=viewer, updated_at=now,
        ))
        if (r.employee.pk, r.date) in existing_pairs:
            report.updated.append(r)
        else:
            report.created.append(r)

    # `unique_fields` is required by SQLite/PostgreSQL but rejected by MySQL
    # (MySQL's ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE matches on any unique constraint
    # automatically). Use the connection feature flag to pick the right shape.
    bulk_kwargs: dict = {
        "update_conflicts": True,
        "update_fields": [
            "shift_type", "shift_attribute",
            "job_location", "work_location",
            "updated_by", "updated_at",
        ],
    }
    if connection.features.supports_update_conflicts_with_target:
        bulk_kwargs["unique_fields"] = ["employee", "date"]

    with transaction.atomic():
        Shift.objects.bulk_create(objs, **bulk_kwargs)

    report.applied = True
    return report


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Template builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_DAYS = 7


def _lookup_shift_names() -> list[str]:
    """Every value that the parser would accept in the Shift column."""
    attr_names = list(
        ShiftAttribute.objects
        .filter(shift_type__is_active=True, shift_type__isnull=False)
        .order_by("shift_type__name", "name")
        .values_list("name", flat=True)
    )
    type_names = list(
        ShiftType.objects
        .filter(is_active=True, has_attribute=False)
        .order_by("category", "name")
        .values_list("name", flat=True)
    )
    # Dedupe while preserving order — attributes first, then leftover types.
    seen = set()
    out: list[str] = []
    for n in attr_names + type_names:
        if n not in seen:
            seen.add(n)
            out.append(n)
    return out


def _template_employees(viewer):
    """Active employees within the viewer's scope, ordered for display."""
    qs = (
        visible_employees(viewer, request=None)
        .filter(is_active=True, employee_id__isnull=False)
        .exclude(employee_id="")
        .order_by("first_name", "last_name")
    )
    return list(qs)


def _template_dates(today: date | None = None) -> list[date]:
    today = today or date.today()
    return [today + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_DAYS)]


def build_xlsx_template(viewer) -> bytes:
    """Generate the prefilled .xlsx template with dropdowns on Shift + Location."""
    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = "Roster"

    employees = _template_employees(viewer)
    dates = _template_dates()
    shift_names = _lookup_shift_names()

    # Row 1: Employee ID | Employee Name | <date> | (empty) | <date> | (empty) | ...
    ws.cell(row=1, column=1, value="Employee ID")
    ws.cell(row=1, column=2, value="Employee Name")
    for i, d in enumerate(dates):
        col = 3 + i * 2
        ws.cell(row=1, column=col, value=d.isoformat())

    # Row 2: empty | empty | Location | Shift | Location | Shift | ...
    for i, _ in enumerate(dates):
        loc_col = 3 + i * 2
        shift_col = loc_col + 1
        ws.cell(row=2, column=loc_col, value="Location")
        ws.cell(row=2, column=shift_col, value="Shift")

    # Rows 3+: one per employee, employee_id as text (keeps leading zeros).
    for ridx, emp in enumerate(employees, start=3):
        eid_cell = ws.cell(row=ridx, column=1, value=emp.employee_id or "")
        eid_cell.number_format = "@"
        ws.cell(row=ridx, column=2, value=emp.display_name)

    # Lookups sheet (hidden) — backs the data validation lists.
    lookups = wb.create_sheet("Lookups")
    lookups.cell(row=1, column=1, value="Shift values")
    lookups.cell(row=1, column=2, value="Locations")
    for i, name in enumerate(shift_names, start=2):
        lookups.cell(row=i, column=1, value=name)
    for i, token in enumerate(LOCATION_TOKENS, start=2):
        lookups.cell(row=i, column=2, value=token)
    lookups.sheet_state = "hidden"

    # Data validations — only attach if we have at least one employee row and
    # at least one shift name; otherwise Excel rejects an empty list reference.
    if employees and dates:
        last_row = 2 + len(employees)
        if shift_names:
            shift_range = (
                f"=Lookups!$A$2:$A${1 + len(shift_names)}"
            )
            shift_dv = DataValidation(
                type="list", formula1=shift_range, allow_blank=True,
            )
            shift_dv.error = "Pick a value from the dropdown."
            shift_dv.errorTitle = "Invalid shift"
            ws.add_data_validation(shift_dv)
            for i, _ in enumerate(dates):
                shift_col = 4 + i * 2
                col_letter = get_column_letter(shift_col)
                shift_dv.add(f"{col_letter}3:{col_letter}{last_row}")

        loc_range = f"=Lookups!$B$2:$B${1 + len(LOCATION_TOKENS)}"
        loc_dv = DataValidation(
            type="list", formula1=loc_range, allow_blank=True,
        )
        loc_dv.error = "Pick a value from the dropdown."
        loc_dv.errorTitle = "Invalid location"
        ws.add_data_validation(loc_dv)
        for i, _ in enumerate(dates):
            loc_col = 3 + i * 2
            col_letter = get_column_letter(loc_col)
            loc_dv.add(f"{col_letter}3:{col_letter}{last_row}")

    # Cosmetic: column widths + freeze panes.
    ws.column_dimensions["A"].width = 14
    ws.column_dimensions["B"].width = 26
    for i, _ in enumerate(dates):
        loc_col = 3 + i * 2
        shift_col = loc_col + 1
        ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(loc_col)].width = 12
        ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(shift_col)].width = 14
    ws.freeze_panes = "C3"

    stream = io.BytesIO()
    wb.save(stream)
    return stream.getvalue()


def build_csv_template(viewer) -> str:
    """Plain-text wide-format CSV — same schema as the xlsx, no dropdowns."""
    employees = _template_employees(viewer)
    dates = _template_dates()

    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out)

    # Row 1: Employee ID | Employee Name | <date> | "" | <date> | "" | ...
    header = ["Employee ID", "Employee Name"]
    for d in dates:
        header.extend([d.isoformat(), ""])
    writer.writerow(header)

    # Row 2: "" | "" | Location | Shift | Location | Shift | ...
    sub = ["", ""]
    for _ in dates:
        sub.extend(["Location", "Shift"])
    writer.writerow(sub)

    # Rows 3+: one row per employee, date cells blank.
    for emp in employees:
        row = [emp.employee_id or "", emp.display_name]
        for _ in dates:
            row.extend(["", ""])
        writer.writerow(row)

    return out.getvalue()


def render_template_response(viewer, fmt: str) -> HttpResponse:
    fmt = (fmt or "").lower()
    today_stamp = date.today().isoformat()
    if fmt == "xlsx":
        body = build_xlsx_template(viewer)
        resp = HttpResponse(
            body,
            content_type=(
                "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"
            ),
        )
        resp["Content-Disposition"] = (
            f'attachment; filename="roster-upload-template-{today_stamp}.xlsx"'
        )
        return resp
    if fmt == "csv":
        body = build_csv_template(viewer)
        resp = HttpResponse(body, content_type="text/csv; charset=utf-8")
        resp["Content-Disposition"] = (
            f'attachment; filename="roster-upload-template-{today_stamp}.csv"'
        )
        return resp
    from django.http import Http404
    raise Http404("Unknown template format.")

    can_edit_all,

    visible_employees,
)
