MAX_RANGE_DAYS = 31


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _monday_of(d: date) -> date:
    return d - timedelta(days=d.weekday())


def _sunday_of(d: date) -> date:
    return _monday_of(d) + timedelta(days=6)


def _parse_date_param(raw: str | None) -> date | None:
    if not raw:
        return None
    return parse_date(raw)


def _parse_int(value):
    try:
        return int(value) if value else None
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _apply_grid_filters(qs, params):
    dept = _parse_int(params.get("department"))
    team = _parse_int(params.get("team"))
    if dept:
        qs = qs.filter(department_id=dept)
    if team:
        qs = qs.filter(team_id=team)
    return qs


def _range_from_request(request):
    """Return (date_from, date_to) — default Mon-Sun of current week."""
    today = date.today()
    df = _parse_date_param(request.GET.get("from")) or _monday_of(today)
    dt = _parse_date_param(request.GET.get("to")) or _sunday_of(today)
    if dt < df:
        dt = df
    if (dt - df).days + 1 > MAX_RANGE_DAYS:
        dt = df + timedelta(days=MAX_RANGE_DAYS - 1)
    return df, dt


def _filter_querystring(params):
    """Build the dept/team filter slug used in hx-post URLs so count
    recomputation stays scoped to the viewed subset."""
    bits = []
    for key in ("department", "team", "from", "to"):
        v = params.get(key)
        if v:
            bits.append(f"{key}={v}")
    return "&".join(bits)


def _resolve_shift_ref(ref):
    """Parse the cell/pattern `<select>` value.

    Returns (shift_type, shift_attribute) — any of the two may be None.
    The caller enforces: empty ref → delete row; non-empty → upsert.
    """
    if not ref:
        return None, None
    try:
        kind, raw_pk = ref.split(":", 1)
        pk = int(raw_pk)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
        raise Http404("Invalid shift reference.")
    if kind == "attr":
        attr = get_object_or_404(
            ShiftAttribute.objects.select_related("shift_type"),
            pk=pk,
        )
        if not attr.shift_type_id:
            raise Http404("Attribute has no parent shift type.")
        return attr.shift_type, attr
    if kind == "type":
        st = get_object_or_404(ShiftType, pk=pk, is_active=True)
        if st.has_attribute:
            raise Http404("Pick a specific attribute for this shift type.")
        return st, None
    raise Http404("Unknown shift reference kind.")


def _active_shift_types_with_attrs():
    return list(
        ShiftType.objects
        .filter(is_active=True)
        .prefetch_related("attributes")
        .order_by("category", "name")
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Weekly grid
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class RosterWeekView(LoginRequiredMixin, View):
    template_name = "roster/week.html"

    def dispatch(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        # Roster grid is a manager / HR / admin tool. Plain employees with no
        # downline and no headed department have nothing to do here — their
        # own row would be read-only anyway since `can_edit_roster_pattern`
        # blocks self-edits. The dynamic-menu sidebar already hides the link
        # for them; this gate covers direct-URL access.
        if request.user.is_authenticated and not has_managed_scope(
            request.user, request=request,
        ):
            raise PermissionDenied("Roster is restricted to managers and HR.")
        return super().dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)

    def get(self, request):
        date_from, date_to = _range_from_request(request)
        days = [date_from + timedelta(days=i) for i in range((date_to - date_from).days + 1)]

        employees_qs = visible_employees(request.user, request=request).select_related(
            "department", "designation", "team", "job_location",
        )
        employees_qs = _apply_grid_filters(employees_qs, request.GET)
        employees = list(employees_qs.order_by("first_name", "last_name"))

        # Materialise missing Shift rows from each employee's weekly pattern.
        services.prefill_shifts_from_pattern(request.user, employees, date_from, date_to)

        # Pull every Shift in one go, including the attribute (for time display).
        shift_rows = (
            Shift.objects
            .filter(employee__in=employees, date__gte=date_from, date__lte=date_to)
            .select_related("shift_type", "shift_attribute")
        )
        shift_map = {(s.employee_id, s.date): s for s in shift_rows}

        holidays = {
            h.date: h for h in Holiday.objects.filter(
                date__gte=date_from, date__lte=date_to, is_active=True,
            )
        }

        # Shift-count aggregation for the sticky header — WORK-category only.
        work_shift_types = list(
            ShiftType.objects
            .filter(is_active=True, category=ShiftType.Category.WORK)
            .order_by("name")
        )
        count_rows = (
            Shift.objects
            .filter(
                employee__in=employees,
                date__gte=date_from, date__lte=date_to,
                shift_type__category=ShiftType.Category.WORK,
            )
            .values("date", "shift_type_id")
            .annotate(n=Count("id"))
        )
        count_map = {(r["date"], r["shift_type_id"]): r["n"] for r in count_rows}

        # Assemble per-day headers.
        day_headers = [
            {
                "date": d,
                "holiday": holidays.get(d),
                "counts": [(st, count_map.get((d, st.pk), 0)) for st in work_shift_types],
            }
            for d in days
        ]

        # Per-row cell list + per-row totals (count by ShiftType.name) +
        # off_count for the "more than 2 OFFs → red employee name" rule.
        all_active_types = _active_shift_types_with_attrs()
        filter_qs = _filter_querystring(request.GET)
        rows = []
        for emp in employees:
            cells = []
            totals_map: dict[str, int] = {}
            off_count = 0
            for d in days:
                shift = shift_map.get((emp.pk, d))
                cells.append({
                    "date": d,
                    "shift": shift,
                    "holiday": holidays.get(d),
                })
                if shift is not None:
                    name = shift.shift_type.name
                    totals_map[name] = totals_map.get(name, 0) + 1
                    if shift.shift_type.category == ShiftType.Category.OFF:
                        off_count += 1
            rows.append({
                "employee": emp,
                "cells": cells,
                "totals": sorted(totals_map.items()),
                "off_count": off_count,
            })

        today = date.today()
        this_mon, this_sun = _monday_of(today), _sunday_of(today)
        next_mon = this_mon + timedelta(days=7)
        next_sun = this_sun + timedelta(days=7)

        ctx = {
            "page_title": "Roster",
            "date_from": date_from,
            "date_to": date_to,
            "days": days,
            "day_headers": day_headers,
            "rows": rows,
            "shift_types": all_active_types,
            "filter_qs": filter_qs,
            "this_mon": this_mon.isoformat(),
            "this_sun": this_sun.isoformat(),
            "next_mon": next_mon.isoformat(),
            "next_sun": next_sun.isoformat(),
            "departments": Department.objects.filter(is_active=True).order_by("name"),
            "teams": Team.objects.filter(is_active=True).order_by("name"),
            "selected_department_id": _parse_int(request.GET.get("department")),
            "selected_team_id": _parse_int(request.GET.get("team")),
            # Pattern-edit gating is per-row; computing once is fine since
            # the same user can edit anyone they can see.
            "can_manage_patterns": can_edit_all(request.user, request=request),
        }
        return render(request, self.template_name, ctx)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cell update — POST-only; returns cell + OOB count
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class CellUpdateView(LoginRequiredMixin, View):
    http_method_names = ["post"]

    def post(self, request, employee_pk, day):
        emp = get_object_or_404(CustomUser, pk=employee_pk, is_active=True)

        # Permission: same scope as weekly pattern — admins anywhere, line
        # managers and dept heads on their managed scope, non-admins never
        # write to their own cells.
        if not can_edit_roster_pattern(request.user, emp, request=request):
            raise PermissionDenied("You can't edit this employee's roster.")

        d = parse_date(day) if isinstance(day, str) else day
        if not d:
            raise Http404("Invalid date.")

        from accounts.locations import resolve_location_choice

        shift_ref = request.POST.get("shift_ref") or request.POST.get("shift_type")
        location_ref = request.POST.get("location_ref")

        # Snapshot the existing row (if any) so we can preserve the field
        # the user *isn't* editing this round.
        existing_shift = (
            Shift.objects.filter(employee=emp, date=d)
            .select_related("job_location", "work_location")
            .first()
        )
        pattern = (
            Roster.objects.filter(employee=emp, weekday=d.weekday())
            .select_related("job_location", "work_location")
            .first()
        )

        # Resolve shift_type / shift_attribute. When location_ref is the
        # only thing being changed (shift_ref absent), preserve the
        # existing/pattern shift instead of clearing.
        if shift_ref is not None:
            st, attr = _resolve_shift_ref(shift_ref)
        elif existing_shift:
            st = existing_shift.shift_type
            attr = existing_shift.shift_attribute
        elif pattern:
            st = pattern.shift_type
            attr = pattern.shift_attribute
        else:
            st, attr = None, None

        # Resolve job_location / work_location.
        if location_ref is not None:
            jl, wl = resolve_location_choice(location_ref)
        elif existing_shift:
            jl = existing_shift.job_location
            wl = existing_shift.work_location
        elif pattern:
            jl = pattern.job_location
            wl = pattern.work_location
        else:
            jl, wl = None, None

        if st is None and attr is None:
            # Genuinely clearing the cell — explicit shift_ref="" with no
            # location_ref or with a blank location_ref both land here.
            Shift.objects.filter(employee=emp, date=d).delete()
        else:
            Shift.objects.update_or_create(
                employee=emp, date=d,
                defaults={
                    "shift_type": st,
                    "shift_attribute": attr,
                    "job_location": jl,
                    "work_location": wl,
                    "updated_by": request.user,
                },
            )
            Shift.objects.filter(
                employee=emp, date=d, added_by__isnull=True,
            ).update(added_by=request.user)

        # Recompute counts scoped to what the user was viewing.
        employees = visible_employees(request.user, request=request)
        employees = _apply_grid_filters(employees, request.GET)
        emp_ids = list(employees.values_list("pk", flat=True))

        work_types = list(
            ShiftType.objects
            .filter(is_active=True, category=ShiftType.Category.WORK)
            .order_by("name")
        )
        day_rows = (
            Shift.objects
            .filter(
                employee_id__in=emp_ids, date=d,
                shift_type__category=ShiftType.Category.WORK,
            )
            .values("shift_type_id").annotate(n=Count("id"))
        )
        day_counts = {r["shift_type_id"]: r["n"] for r in day_rows}
        day_header = {
            "date": d,
            "counts": [(st, day_counts.get(st.pk, 0)) for st in work_types],
        }

        shift = (
            Shift.objects.filter(employee=emp, date=d)
            .select_related("shift_type", "shift_attribute")
            .first()
        )
        holiday = Holiday.objects.filter(date=d, is_active=True).first()

        all_active_types = _active_shift_types_with_attrs()

        cell_ctx = {
            "employee": emp,
            "date": d,
            "shift": shift,
            "holiday": holiday,
            "oob": False,
            "shift_types": all_active_types,
            "filter_qs": _filter_querystring(request.GET),
        }
        count_ctx = {"day_header": day_header, "oob": True}

        # Recompute this employee's row totals + off_count across the whole
        # visible week so the right-side Total column and the employee-name
        # color stay in sync after an HTMX cell update.
        date_from, date_to = _range_from_request(request)
        row_shifts = (
            Shift.objects
            .filter(employee=emp, date__gte=date_from, date__lte=date_to)
            .select_related("shift_type")
        )
        totals_map: dict[str, int] = {}
        off_count = 0
        for s in row_shifts:
            totals_map[s.shift_type.name] = totals_map.get(s.shift_type.name, 0) + 1
            if s.shift_type.category == ShiftType.Category.OFF:
                off_count += 1
        row_total_ctx = {
            "employee": emp,
            "totals": sorted(totals_map.items()),
            "oob": True,
        }
        emp_name_ctx = {
            "employee": emp,
            "off_count": off_count,
            "can_manage_patterns": can_edit_all(request.user, request=request),
            "oob": True,
        }

        body = (
            render_to_string("roster/_cell.html", cell_ctx, request=request)
            + render_to_string("roster/_count_cell.html", count_ctx, request=request)
            + render_to_string("roster/_row_total.html", row_total_ctx, request=request)
            + render_to_string("roster/_emp_name.html", emp_name_ctx, request=request)
        )
        return HttpResponse(body)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Weekly pattern edit page
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_WEEKDAY_LABELS = {
    0: "Monday", 1: "Tuesday", 2: "Wednesday", 3: "Thursday",
    4: "Friday", 5: "Saturday", 6: "Sunday",
}


class RosterPatternView(LoginRequiredMixin, View):
    template_name = "roster/pattern_form.html"
    http_method_names = ["get", "post"]

    def dispatch(self, request, employee_pk, *args, **kwargs):
        self.employee = get_object_or_404(CustomUser, pk=employee_pk)
        if not can_edit_roster_pattern(request.user, self.employee, request=request):
            raise PermissionDenied("You can't edit this employee's weekly pattern.")
        return super().dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)

    def _existing_rows(self):
        return {
            r.weekday: r for r in
            Roster.objects.filter(employee=self.employee).select_related(
                "shift_attribute", "job_location", "work_location",
            )
        }

    def _initial(self):
        from accounts.locations import resolve_to_dropdown_choice
        existing = self._existing_rows()
        initial = []
        for wd in range(7):
            row = existing.get(wd)
            if row is None:
                initial.append({"weekday": wd, "shift_ref": ""})
                continue
            if row.shift_attribute_id:
                ref = f"attr:{row.shift_attribute_id}"
            else:
                ref = f"type:{row.shift_type_id}"
            initial.append({
                "weekday": wd,
                "shift_ref": ref,
                "location": resolve_to_dropdown_choice(
                    row.job_location, row.work_location,
                ),
            })
        return initial

    def _formset_cls(self):
        return formset_factory(RosterPatternRowForm, extra=0, min_num=7, max_num=7, validate_min=True, validate_max=True)

    def get(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        Formset = self._formset_cls()
        formset = Formset(initial=self._initial())
        return self._render(request, formset)

    def post(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        from accounts.locations import resolve_location_choice
        Formset = self._formset_cls()
        formset = Formset(request.POST)
        if formset.is_valid():
            for form in formset.forms:
                wd = form.cleaned_data.get("weekday")
                ref = form.cleaned_data.get("shift_ref")
                location = form.cleaned_data.get("location") or ""
                st, attr = _resolve_shift_ref(ref)
                if st is None and attr is None:
                    Roster.objects.filter(employee=self.employee, weekday=wd).delete()
                    continue
                jl, wl = resolve_location_choice(location)
                Roster.objects.update_or_create(
                    employee=self.employee, weekday=wd,
                    defaults={
                        "shift_type": st,
                        "shift_attribute": attr,
                        "job_location": jl,
                        "work_location": wl,
                        "updated_by": request.user,
                    },
                )
                Roster.objects.filter(
                    employee=self.employee, weekday=wd, added_by__isnull=True,
                ).update(added_by=request.user)
            messages.success(request, f"Weekly pattern saved for {self.employee.display_name}.")
            return redirect("employee_detail", pk=self.employee.pk)
        return self._render(request, formset)

    def _render(self, request, formset):
        # Attach human labels to each form (formset preserves order Mon→Sun).
        for i, form in enumerate(formset.forms):
            form.weekday_label = _WEEKDAY_LABELS[i]
        ctx = {
            "employee": self.employee,
            "formset": formset,
            "page_title": f"Weekly pattern — {self.employee.display_name}",
        }
        return render(request, self.template_name, ctx)

from django import forms

from accounts.locations import LOCATION_DROPDOWN_CHOICES
from core.forms import StyledMixin
from roster.models import ShiftType


class ShiftTypeForm(forms.ModelForm, StyledMixin):
    class Meta:
        model = ShiftType
        fields = (
            "name", "description",
            "category", "shift_timezone",
            "shift_start_time", "shift_end_time",
            "color", "has_attribute", "is_active",
        )

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        for time_field in ("shift_start_time", "shift_end_time"):
            self.fields[time_field].widget = forms.TimeInput(
                attrs={"type": "time", "placeholder": "HH:MM"},
                format="%H:%M",
            )
        self.style_widgets()


class RosterPatternRowForm(forms.Form, StyledMixin):
    """One row in the seven-weekday pattern formset.

    `weekday` is hidden. `shift_ref` encodes the selected option as either
    `type:<pk>` (shift type without variants) or `attr:<pk>` (specific
    attribute). Empty = clear the row.
    """

    weekday = forms.IntegerField(widget=forms.HiddenInput())
    shift_ref = forms.CharField(required=False, widget=forms.Select(), label="Shift")
    location = forms.ChoiceField(
        choices=[("", "— default —"), *LOCATION_DROPDOWN_CHOICES],
        required=False,
        label="Location",
    )

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        # Widget choices are built dynamically so optgroups + attribute
        # variants appear together in one dropdown.
        choices = [("", "—")]
        shift_types = (
            ShiftType.objects.filter(is_active=True)
            .prefetch_related("attributes")
            .order_by("category", "name")
        )
        by_cat: dict[str, list] = {}
        for st in shift_types:
            cat = st.get_category_display()
            if st.has_attribute:
                for attr in st.attributes.all().order_by("start_time", "name"):
                    label = attr.name
                    if attr.start_time:
                        label += f" ({attr.start_time.strftime('%H:%M')}–{attr.end_time.strftime('%H:%M')})"
                    by_cat.setdefault(cat, []).append((f"attr:{attr.pk}", label))
            else:
                label = st.name
                if st.shift_start_time:
                    label += f" ({st.shift_start_time.strftime('%H:%M')}–{st.shift_end_time.strftime('%H:%M')})"
                by_cat.setdefault(cat, []).append((f"type:{st.pk}", label))

        # (group_label, [(value, label), ...]) tuples for Django's optgroup rendering.
        choices.extend(list(by_cat.items()))
        self.fields["shift_ref"].widget.choices = choices
        self.style_widgets()

"""Roster upload — page + template download."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date

from django.contrib import messages
from django.contrib.auth.mixins import LoginRequiredMixin
from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied
from django.http import HttpResponse
from django.shortcuts import render
from django.views import View

from accounts.permissions import has_managed_scope, visible_employee_pks
from roster.upload import (
    ApplyReport,
    apply_upload,
    parse_upload,
    render_template_response,
)


MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024   # 5 MB

PAGE_TEMPLATE = "roster/upload.html"
FRAGMENT_TEMPLATE = "roster/_upload_report.html"


class _ManagedScopeRequired(LoginRequiredMixin, View):
    """Mirror the gate at roster.views.RosterWeekView.dispatch."""

    def dispatch(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        if request.user.is_authenticated and not has_managed_scope(
            request.user, request=request,
        ):
            raise PermissionDenied(
                "Roster upload is restricted to managers and HR."
            )
        return super().dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)


def _is_htmx(request) -> bool:
    """django-htmx middleware sets `request.htmx` truthy on htmx requests."""
    return bool(getattr(request, "htmx", False))


def _respond(request, ctx: dict) -> HttpResponse:
    """Render the result fragment for HTMX requests; the full page for plain
    submits and GETs. Either way the file input in the form is preserved
    (HTMX path: the form element isn't swapped; full-page path: legacy
    behavior, file would need re-attaching — only used as a JS-off fallback)."""
    if _is_htmx(request):
        return render(request, FRAGMENT_TEMPLATE, ctx)
    return render(request, PAGE_TEMPLATE, ctx)


class UploadRosterView(_ManagedScopeRequired):
    def get(self, request) -> HttpResponse:
        return render(request, PAGE_TEMPLATE, {"page_title": "Upload roster"})

    def post(self, request) -> HttpResponse:
        upload = request.FILES.get("file")
        action = (request.POST.get("action") or "apply").lower()
        preview = action == "preview"

        ctx: dict = {"page_title": "Upload roster", "preview": preview}

        if upload is None:
            ctx["inline_error"] = "Choose a .xlsx or .csv file before submitting."
            if not _is_htmx(request):
                messages.error(request, ctx["inline_error"])
            return _respond(request, ctx)

        if upload.size > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES:
            ctx["inline_error"] = (
                f"File is too large ({upload.size:,} bytes). Limit is 5 MB."
            )
            if not _is_htmx(request):
                messages.error(request, ctx["inline_error"])
            return _respond(request, ctx)

        try:
            parsed, parse_errors, dup_errors = parse_upload(
                upload, upload.name, today=date.today(),
            )
        except ValueError as exc:
            # Header-level / wholly-malformed file → single banner error.
            ctx["inline_error"] = str(exc)
            if not _is_htmx(request):
                messages.error(request, str(exc))
            return _respond(request, ctx)

        # Build a baseline report so the template can render parse errors even
        # when nothing was applied.
        report = ApplyReport(parse_errors=parse_errors, duplicates=dup_errors)

        if parse_errors or dup_errors:
            ctx["report"] = report
            ctx["aborted"] = True
            if not _is_htmx(request):
                messages.error(
                    request,
                    "Upload aborted — fix the errors below and re-upload.",
                )
            return _respond(request, ctx)

        if preview:
            # Dry-run: build a synthetic report without writing.
            ctx.update({
                "report": report,
                "parsed_preview": parsed,
                "preview": True,
            })
            if not _is_htmx(request):
                messages.info(
                    request,
                    f"Preview only — {len(parsed)} row(s) would be applied.",
                )
            return _respond(request, ctx)

        visible_pks = visible_employee_pks(request.user, request=request)
        report = apply_upload(request.user, parsed, visible_pks)
        ctx["report"] = report

        if not _is_htmx(request):
            if report.total_writes:
                messages.success(
                    request,
                    f"Applied {report.total_writes} row(s): "
                    f"{len(report.created)} created, {len(report.updated)} updated."
                    + (
                        f" {len(report.skipped_scope)} skipped (outside scope)."
                        if report.skipped_scope else ""
                    ),
                )
            elif report.skipped_scope:
                messages.warning(
                    request,
                    "Nothing applied — every row was outside your managed scope.",
                )
            else:
                messages.info(request, "No rows to apply.")

        return _respond(request, ctx)


class UploadTemplateView(_ManagedScopeRequired):
    http_method_names = ["get"]

    def get(self, request, fmt) -> HttpResponse:
        return render_template_response(request.user, fmt)

"""Read-only Roster API consumed by TimeLy (Laravel).

Auth: `Authorization: Token <TIMELY_API_TOKEN>` — the token is stored in
Orbis's .env and TimeLy's .env; no per-user DRF tokens needed for MVP.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, datetime

from django.conf import settings
from rest_framework import authentication, exceptions, serializers
from rest_framework.exceptions import NotFound, ValidationError
from rest_framework.generics import ListAPIView

from accounts.locations import office_bucket

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auth
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class _ServiceAccount:
    """Stand-in principal representing the TimeLy service account."""

    is_authenticated = True
    is_active = True
    is_staff = False
    is_superuser = False
    pk = 0

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return "timely-service-account"


class TimelyTokenAuthentication(authentication.BaseAuthentication):
    """Match `Authorization: Token <TIMELY_API_TOKEN>` against settings."""

    keyword = "Token"

    def authenticate(self, request):
        header = authentication.get_authorization_header(request).split()
        if not header or header[0].lower() != self.keyword.lower().encode():
            return None
        if len(header) != 2:
            raise exceptions.AuthenticationFailed("Invalid token header.")
        try:
            token = header[1].decode()
        except UnicodeError as exc:
            raise exceptions.AuthenticationFailed("Malformed token.") from exc

        expected = getattr(settings, "TIMELY_API_TOKEN", "")
        if not expected:
            raise exceptions.AuthenticationFailed("TIMELY_API_TOKEN is not configured.")
        if token != expected:
            raise exceptions.AuthenticationFailed("Invalid token.")
        return (_ServiceAccount(), token)

    def authenticate_header(self, request):
        return "Token"

def _work_location_code(work_location) -> str | None:
    """Map a ``WorkLocation`` row to a short code: WFO / WFH / HYB / None."""
    if work_location is None:
        return None
    name = (work_location.name or "").upper()
    if "WFH" in name or "HOME" in name:
        return "WFH"
    if "HYBRID" in name:
        return "HYB"
    if "WFO" in name or "OFFICE" in name:
        return "WFO"
    return None


class TimelyShiftSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    """Lean shape exposed to TimeLy. One row per concrete ``Shift``.

    Fields documented in /home/smrashel/.claude/plans/harmonic-sniffing-flute.md.
    """

    working_day = serializers.DateField(source="date", format="%Y-%m-%d")
    employee_id = serializers.CharField(source="employee.employee_id")
    name = serializers.CharField(source="employee.display_name")
    shift_attribute = serializers.SerializerMethodField()
    shift_start_time = serializers.SerializerMethodField()
    shift_end_time = serializers.SerializerMethodField()
    office_location = serializers.SerializerMethodField()
    work_location = serializers.SerializerMethodField()

    # ----- attribute / type fallback -----

    def get_shift_attribute(self, obj: Shift) -> str:
        if obj.shift_attribute_id and obj.shift_attribute is not None:
            return obj.shift_attribute.name
        return obj.shift_type.name

    # ----- times: prefer attribute, fall back to type -----

    def _resolved_times(self, obj: Shift) -> tuple:
        sa = obj.shift_attribute
        if sa is not None and sa.start_time is not None:
            return sa.start_time, sa.end_time
        return obj.shift_type.shift_start_time, obj.shift_type.shift_end_time

    def get_shift_start_time(self, obj: Shift) -> str | None:
        start, _ = self._resolved_times(obj)
        return start.strftime("%H:%M") if start else None

    def get_shift_end_time(self, obj: Shift) -> str | None:
        _, end = self._resolved_times(obj)
        return end.strftime("%H:%M") if end else None

    # ----- locations: only meaningful for WORK shifts -----

    def get_office_location(self, obj: Shift) -> str | None:
        if obj.shift_type.category != ShiftType.Category.WORK:
            return None
        jl = obj.job_location or obj.employee.job_location
        if jl is None:
            return None
        bucket = office_bucket(jl)
        if bucket in ("MBD", "MHK", "RAOWA"):
            return bucket
        return None

    def get_work_location(self, obj: Shift) -> str | None:
        if obj.shift_type.category != ShiftType.Category.WORK:
            return None
        wl = obj.work_location or obj.employee.work_location
        return _work_location_code(wl)

class _BaseAPI:
    authentication_classes = [TimelyTokenAuthentication]
    permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]


def _parse_iso_date(value: str, field_name: str) -> date:
    """Parse YYYY-MM-DD or raise DRF ``ValidationError`` keyed by field name."""
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(value, "%Y-%m-%d").date()
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValidationError(
            {field_name: "Bad format, expected YYYY-MM-DD"}
        )


_SHIFT_SELECT_RELATED = (
    "shift_type",
    "shift_attribute",
    "job_location",
    "work_location",
    "employee",
    "employee__job_location",
    "employee__work_location",
)


class ShiftTypeListAPI(_BaseAPI, ListAPIView):
    queryset = (
        ShiftType.objects.filter(is_active=True)
        .prefetch_related("attributes")
        .order_by("category", "name")
    )
    serializer_class = ShiftTypeSerializer


class HolidayListAPI(_BaseAPI, ListAPIView):
    serializer_class = HolidaySerializer

    def get_queryset(self):
        qs = Holiday.objects.filter(is_active=True).order_by("date")
        year = self.request.query_params.get("year")
        if year:
            try:
                qs = qs.filter(date__year=int(year))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                pass
        return qs


class EmployeeListAPI(_BaseAPI, ListAPIView):
    serializer_class = EmployeeSerializer

    def get_queryset(self):
        qs = (
            CustomUser.objects.all()
            .select_related("department", "designation", "team", "job_location", "work_location")
            .order_by("first_name", "last_name")
        )
        is_active = self.request.query_params.get("is_active")
        if is_active is not None:
            qs = qs.filter(is_active=is_active.lower() in ("1", "true", "yes"))
        return qs


class DailyRosterAPI(_BaseAPI, ListAPIView):
    """``GET /api/v1/roster/?date=YYYY-MM-DD`` — all concrete Shift rows for a day."""

    serializer_class = TimelyShiftSerializer
    pagination_class = None

    def get_queryset(self):
        date_str = self.request.query_params.get("date")
        if not date_str:
            raise ValidationError(
                {"date": "Required, format YYYY-MM-DD"}
            )
        day = _parse_iso_date(date_str, "date")
        return (
            Shift.objects
            .filter(
                date=day,
                employee__is_active=True,
                employee__employee_id__isnull=False,
            )
            .exclude(employee__employee_id="")
            .select_related(*_SHIFT_SELECT_RELATED)
            .order_by("employee__first_name", "employee__last_name")
        )


class EmployeeRangeRosterAPI(_BaseAPI, ListAPIView):
    """``GET /api/v1/roster/<str:employee_id>/?start_date=&end_date=``.

    Path param is the human ``CustomUser.employee_id`` string (e.g. ``"917"``),
    not the Orbis UUID. Range is required and capped at 92 days.
    """

    serializer_class = TimelyShiftSerializer
    pagination_class = None

    _MAX_RANGE_DAYS = 92

    def get_queryset(self):
        employee_id = self.kwargs["employee_id"]
        start_str = self.request.query_params.get("start_date")
        end_str = self.request.query_params.get("end_date")

        errors = {}
        if not start_str:
            errors["start_date"] = "Required, format YYYY-MM-DD"
        if not end_str:
            errors["end_date"] = "Required, format YYYY-MM-DD"
        if errors:
            raise ValidationError(errors)

        start = _parse_iso_date(start_str, "start_date")
        end = _parse_iso_date(end_str, "end_date")
        if end < start:
            raise ValidationError(
                {"end_date": "Must be on or after start_date"}
            )
        if (end - start).days > self._MAX_RANGE_DAYS:
            raise ValidationError(
                {"end_date": f"Date range exceeds {self._MAX_RANGE_DAYS} days"}
            )

        if not CustomUser.objects.filter(
            employee_id=employee_id, is_active=True,
        ).exists():
            raise NotFound(
                f"No active employee with employee_id={employee_id}"
            )

        return (
            Shift.objects
            .filter(
                employee__employee_id=employee_id,
                employee__is_active=True,
                date__gte=start, date__lte=end,
            )
            .select_related(*_SHIFT_SELECT_RELATED)
            .order_by("date")
        )

def _ensure_groups():

                 "Line Managers", "Department Heads", "All Employees"):

        email=email, username=email, password="x",
        first_name=email.split("@")[0].title(), last_name="T",

def _seed_shifts():
    eve = ShiftType.objects.create(
        name="EVE", category=ShiftType.Category.WORK,
        shift_start_time=time(14, 0), shift_end_time=time(23, 0),
    )
    eve_attr = ShiftAttribute.objects.create(
        shift_type=eve, name="EVE 1-10",
        start_time=time(13, 0), end_time=time(22, 0),
    )
    off = ShiftType.objects.create(
        name="OFF", category=ShiftType.Category.OFF,
        is_working_shift=False,
    )
    return eve, eve_attr, off

class UploadHelpersTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _ensure_groups()
        cls.eve, cls.eve_attr, cls.off = _seed_shifts()

    def test_resolve_shift_attribute_wins(self):
        st, attr = _resolve_shift("EVE 1-10")
        self.assertEqual(st, self.eve)
        self.assertEqual(attr, self.eve_attr)

    def test_resolve_shift_falls_back_to_type(self):
        st, attr = _resolve_shift("off")    # case-insensitive
        self.assertEqual(st, self.off)
        self.assertIsNone(attr)

    def test_resolve_shift_type_with_attribute_must_pick_variant(self):
        # EVE has at least one attribute → can't pick the bare type.
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _resolve_shift("EVE")

    def test_resolve_shift_unknown(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _resolve_shift("FAKESHIFT")

    def test_resolve_shift_empty(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _resolve_shift("")

    def test_resolve_location_empty(self):
        jl, wl = _resolve_location("")
        self.assertIsNone(jl)
        self.assertIsNone(wl)

    def test_resolve_location_wfh(self):
        jl, wl = _resolve_location("wfh")
        self.assertIsNone(jl)
        self.assertIsNotNone(wl)

    def test_resolve_location_office(self):
        jl, wl = _resolve_location("MHK")
        self.assertIsNotNone(jl)
        self.assertIsNotNone(wl)

    def test_resolve_location_unknown(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _resolve_location("XYZ")

    def test_coerce_employee_id_int(self):
        self.assertEqual(_coerce_employee_id(539), "539")

    def test_coerce_employee_id_float_int(self):
        self.assertEqual(_coerce_employee_id(539.0), "539")

    def test_coerce_employee_id_float_decimal_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _coerce_employee_id(539.5)

    def test_coerce_employee_id_string(self):
        self.assertEqual(_coerce_employee_id("  E0042  "), "E0042")

    def test_coerce_employee_id_empty(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _coerce_employee_id("   ")

    def test_parse_cell_date_iso(self):
        d = _parse_cell_date("2026-05-18", today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        self.assertEqual(d, date(2026, 5, 18))

    def test_parse_cell_date_native(self):
        d = _parse_cell_date(datetime(2026, 5, 18, 0, 0), today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        self.assertEqual(d, date(2026, 5, 18))

    def test_parse_cell_date_bad_format(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _parse_cell_date("18-05-2026", today=date(2026, 5, 13))

    def test_parse_cell_date_too_far(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            _parse_cell_date("2099-01-01", today=date(2026, 5, 13))

class UploadParseAndApplyTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _ensure_groups()
        cls.eve, cls.eve_attr, cls.off = _seed_shifts()

        # Manager + downline.
        cls.manager = _user("mgr@example.com", "M001")
        cls.alice = _user("alice@example.com", "100")
        cls.bob = _user("bob@example.com", "101")
        cls.outsider = _user("out@example.com", "999")

        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.alice, reports_to=cls.manager)
        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.bob, reports_to=cls.manager)
        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.outsider, reports_to=None)

    def _csv(self, lines: list[str]) -> io.BytesIO:
        return io.BytesIO("\n".join(lines).encode("utf-8"))

    def test_parse_happy_csv(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,,2026-05-19,",
            ",,Location,Shift,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,EVE 1-10,MHK,EVE 1-10",
            "101,Bob T,,EVE 1-10,,OFF",
        ])
        parsed, errors, dups = parse_upload(
            f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
        )
        self.assertEqual(errors, [])
        self.assertEqual(dups, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 4)
        by_emp = {(p.employee_id, p.date.isoformat()) for p in parsed}
        self.assertIn(("100", "2026-05-18"), by_emp)
        self.assertIn(("101", "2026-05-19"), by_emp)
        bob_off = next(p for p in parsed if p.employee_id == "101" and p.date == date(2026, 5, 19))
        self.assertEqual(bob_off.shift_type, self.off)
        self.assertIsNone(bob_off.shift_attribute)
        self.assertIsNone(bob_off.job_location)
        self.assertIsNone(bob_off.work_location)

    def test_parse_skips_empty_pairs(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,,2026-05-19,",
            ",,Location,Shift,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,,,,",            # entirely blank — produces 0 rows
        ])
        parsed, errors, dups = parse_upload(
            f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
        )
        self.assertEqual(parsed, [])
        self.assertEqual(errors, [])
        self.assertEqual(dups, [])

    def test_parse_location_without_shift_errors(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,",
        ])
        parsed, errors, dups = parse_upload(
            f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
        )
        self.assertEqual(parsed, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(errors), 1)
        self.assertIn("Location filled but Shift", errors[0].message)

    def test_parse_unknown_shift_errors(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,FAKESHIFT",
        ])
        parsed, errors, _ = parse_upload(
            f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
        )
        self.assertEqual(parsed, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(errors), 1)
        self.assertIn("Unknown shift", errors[0].message)

    def test_parse_unknown_location_errors(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,XYZ,EVE 1-10",
        ])
        parsed, errors, _ = parse_upload(
            f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
        )
        self.assertEqual(parsed, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(errors), 1)
        self.assertIn("Unknown location", errors[0].message)

    def test_parse_bad_employee_id_errors(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "999999,Bad Person,MHK,EVE 1-10",
        ])
        parsed, errors, _ = parse_upload(
            f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
        )
        self.assertEqual(parsed, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(errors), 1)
        self.assertIn("No active employee", errors[0].message)

    def test_parse_duplicate_in_file(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,EVE 1-10",
            "100,Alice T (again),MHK,EVE 1-10",
        ])
        parsed, errors, dups = parse_upload(
            f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 1)
        self.assertEqual(errors, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(dups), 1)
        self.assertIn("Duplicate", dups[0].message)

    def test_parse_bad_subheader_aborts(self):
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Wrong,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,EVE 1-10",
        ])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            parse_upload(f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))

    def test_apply_create_then_update(self):
        from accounts.permissions import visible_employee_pks

        # First pass: create 2 rows.
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,,2026-05-19,",
            ",,Location,Shift,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,EVE 1-10,MHK,EVE 1-10",
        ])
        parsed, _, _ = parse_upload(f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        visible_pks = visible_employee_pks(self.manager)
        report = apply_upload(self.manager, parsed, visible_pks)
        self.assertEqual(len(report.created), 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(report.updated), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(report.skipped_scope), 0)
        self.assertEqual(Shift.objects.filter(employee=self.alice).count(), 2)

        # Second pass: same (employee, date), different shift → updates.
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,,OFF",
        ])
        parsed, _, _ = parse_upload(f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        report2 = apply_upload(self.manager, parsed, visible_pks)
        self.assertEqual(len(report2.created), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(report2.updated), 1)
        s = Shift.objects.get(employee=self.alice, date=date(2026, 5, 18))
        self.assertEqual(s.shift_type, self.off)
        self.assertIsNone(s.shift_attribute)
        self.assertIsNone(s.job_location)
        self.assertIsNone(s.work_location)
        self.assertEqual(s.updated_by, self.manager)

    def test_apply_outside_scope_is_skipped(self):
        from accounts.permissions import visible_employee_pks

        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,EVE 1-10",          # in scope
            "999,Outsider,MHK,EVE 1-10",          # NOT in scope
        ])
        parsed, _, _ = parse_upload(f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        visible_pks = visible_employee_pks(self.manager)
        report = apply_upload(self.manager, parsed, visible_pks)
        self.assertEqual(len(report.created), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(report.skipped_scope), 1)
        self.assertEqual(report.skipped_scope[0].raw["Employee ID"], "999")
        # Only the alice row should have landed.
        self.assertFalse(Shift.objects.filter(employee=self.outsider).exists())

    def test_apply_added_by_set_on_create(self):
        from accounts.permissions import visible_employee_pks
        f = self._csv([
            "Employee ID,Employee Name,2026-05-18,",
            ",,Location,Shift",
            "100,Alice T,MHK,EVE 1-10",
        ])
        parsed, _, _ = parse_upload(f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        apply_upload(self.manager, parsed, visible_employee_pks(self.manager))
        s = Shift.objects.get(employee=self.alice, date=date(2026, 5, 18))
        self.assertEqual(s.added_by, self.manager)
        self.assertEqual(s.updated_by, self.manager)


@override_settings(
    STORAGES={
        "default": {"BACKEND": "django.core.files.storage.FileSystemStorage"},
        "staticfiles": {"BACKEND": "django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.StaticFilesStorage"},
    },
)
class UploadScalePerfTests(TestCase):
    """Query-count budget for the 700-employee × 7-day department-head case.

    Asserts a hard upper bound so a future refactor can't silently regress
    the cached-lookup path back into per-cell DB hits.
    """

    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _ensure_groups()
        cls.eve, cls.eve_attr, cls.off = _seed_shifts()
        cls.manager = _user("mgr@example.com", "M001")
        # 50 employees is enough to surface a per-row/per-cell N+1 — the
        # cached path stays at constant query count regardless of N.
        cls.employees = []
        for i in range(50):
            u = _user(f"emp{i}@example.com", f"E{i:03d}")
            JobInfo.objects.create(employee=u, reports_to=cls.manager)
            cls.employees.append(u)

    def _wide_csv(self, employees, num_days: int) -> io.BytesIO:
        base = date(2026, 5, 18)
        date_headers = [(base + __import__("datetime").timedelta(days=i)).isoformat()
                        for i in range(num_days)]
        line1 = ["Employee ID", "Employee Name"]
        for d in date_headers:
            line1.extend([d, ""])
        line2 = ["", ""]
        for _ in date_headers:
            line2.extend(["Location", "Shift"])
        lines = [",".join(line1), ",".join(line2)]
        for e in employees:
            row = [e.employee_id, e.display_name]
            for _ in date_headers:
                row.extend(["MHK", "EVE 1-10"])
            lines.append(",".join(row))
        return io.BytesIO("\n".join(lines).encode("utf-8"))

    def test_parse_query_budget_is_constant(self):
        """Parsing 50 employees × 7 days = 350 cells must use a fixed number
        of queries (the cache build), not per-cell queries.
        """
        f = self._wide_csv(self.employees, num_days=7)
        from django.test.utils import CaptureQueriesContext
        from django.db import connection

        with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as ctx:
            parsed, errors, dups = parse_upload(
                f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13),
            )

        self.assertEqual(len(parsed), 350)
        self.assertEqual(errors, [])
        self.assertEqual(dups, [])
        # Budget: 4 query for holidays/employees/shift-attrs/shift-types +
        # ~5-30 for the location-cache build (each token resolves to an
        # existing canonical row in 1 query on prod; cold test DB hits
        # get_or_create paths that add a few inserts). Whatever the absolute
        # number, it must be CONSTANT, not scale with the 350 cells.
        # 60 is a comfortable ceiling that still catches a per-cell regression
        # (which would put us in the hundreds at minimum).
        self.assertLess(
            len(ctx.captured_queries), 60,
            f"parse_upload used {len(ctx.captured_queries)} queries for 350 cells — "
            f"per-cell lookup regressed.\n" +
            "\n".join(q["sql"][:120] for q in ctx.captured_queries)
        )

    def test_apply_query_budget_is_constant(self):
        """Applying 350 rows must use one bulk INSERT-ON-CONFLICT, not 350
        update_or_create calls.
        """
        from accounts.permissions import visible_employee_pks
        f = self._wide_csv(self.employees, num_days=7)
        parsed, _, _ = parse_upload(f, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))

        visible_pks = visible_employee_pks(self.manager)
        from django.test.utils import CaptureQueriesContext
        from django.db import connection
        with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as ctx:
            report = apply_upload(self.manager, parsed, visible_pks)

        self.assertEqual(len(report.created), 350)
        self.assertEqual(Shift.objects.count(), 350)
        # Budget: pre-existing-pair lookup (1) + bulk_create with conflicts (1)
        # wrapped in a SAVEPOINT begin/release (2) ≈ 4–6 queries.
        self.assertLess(
            len(ctx.captured_queries), 12,
            f"apply_upload used {len(ctx.captured_queries)} queries — "
            f"bulk path regressed.\n" +
            "\n".join(q["sql"][:120] for q in ctx.captured_queries)
        )

    def test_apply_overwrite_path_is_also_bulk(self):
        """A second apply over the same rows (pure overwrite path) keeps the
        same query budget — no per-row update fan-out.
        """
        from accounts.permissions import visible_employee_pks
        visible_pks = visible_employee_pks(self.manager)

        # First apply: create.
        f1 = self._wide_csv(self.employees, num_days=7)
        parsed1, _, _ = parse_upload(f1, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        apply_upload(self.manager, parsed1, visible_pks)
        self.assertEqual(Shift.objects.count(), 350)

        # Second apply: overwrite.
        f2 = self._wide_csv(self.employees, num_days=7)
        parsed2, _, _ = parse_upload(f2, "roster.csv", today=date(2026, 5, 13))
        from django.test.utils import CaptureQueriesContext
        from django.db import connection
        with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as ctx:
            report = apply_upload(self.manager, parsed2, visible_pks)

        self.assertEqual(len(report.created), 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(report.updated), 350)
        self.assertEqual(Shift.objects.count(), 350)
        self.assertLess(
            len(ctx.captured_queries), 12,
            f"overwrite apply used {len(ctx.captured_queries)} queries — "
            f"bulk path regressed.\n" +
            "\n".join(q["sql"][:120] for q in ctx.captured_queries)
        )

class UploadTemplateBuilderTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _ensure_groups()
        cls.eve, cls.eve_attr, cls.off = _seed_shifts()
        cls.manager = _user("mgr@example.com", "M001")
        cls.alice = _user("alice@example.com", "100")
        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.alice, reports_to=cls.manager)

    def test_csv_template_has_two_header_rows(self):
        body = build_csv_template(self.manager)
        lines = body.splitlines()
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(lines), 2)
        self.assertTrue(lines[0].startswith("Employee ID,Employee Name,"))
        self.assertIn("Location", lines[1])
        self.assertIn("Shift", lines[1])
        # Includes Alice as a downline row.
        self.assertTrue(any("100,Alice" in ln or ln.startswith("100,") for ln in lines))

    def test_xlsx_template_has_dropdowns(self):
        body = build_xlsx_template(self.manager)
        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(io.BytesIO(body))
        self.assertIn("Roster", wb.sheetnames)
        self.assertIn("Lookups", wb.sheetnames)
        ws = wb["Roster"]
        # Row 1 cols: Employee ID | Employee Name | <date> | (empty) | ...
        self.assertEqual(ws.cell(row=1, column=1).value, "Employee ID")
        self.assertEqual(ws.cell(row=1, column=2).value, "Employee Name")
        # Row 2: Location / Shift sub-headers on the date pairs (cols 3+).
        self.assertEqual(ws.cell(row=2, column=3).value, "Location")
        self.assertEqual(ws.cell(row=2, column=4).value, "Shift")
        # Alice prefilled on row 3.
        self.assertEqual(ws.cell(row=3, column=1).value, "100")
        # Lookups sheet hidden.
        self.assertEqual(wb["Lookups"].sheet_state, "hidden")
        # Lookups B column = location tokens.
        loc_col = [
            wb["Lookups"].cell(row=i, column=2).value
            for i in range(2, 2 + len(LOCATION_DROPDOWN_VALUES))
        ]
        self.assertEqual(set(loc_col), set(LOCATION_DROPDOWN_VALUES))
        # At least one data validation attached.
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(ws.data_validations.dataValidation), 1)

# ==========================================
# FILE: ./roster/management/commands/seed_shift_attributes.py
# ==========================================
"""Seed ShiftAttribute rows for production.

Recreates the time-variant attributes (MOR 7-4, EVE 1-10, NIG 9-7, etc.)
from SEBPO's existing roster system on top of the new production ShiftTypes
(MOR, EVE, NIG, CUST + leave/holiday/off types).

ShiftType lookups are by **name**, not PK — so this works the same against
dev, staging, or production regardless of seed-row IDs.

Idempotent: existing (shift_type, name) pairs are left alone. Missing ones
are created. Use ``--dry-run`` to preview.

Usage::

    manage.py seed_shift_attributes --dry-run
    manage.py seed_shift_attributes
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import time

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django.db import transaction

from roster.models import ShiftAttribute, ShiftType


# (parent_shift_type_name, attribute_name, start_time, end_time)
# `None`/`None` for start/end means a non-time variant (leave/off mirror).
SEED: list[tuple[str, str, time | None, time | None]] = [
    # ── Working shifts: time variants ──
    ("MOR",  "MOR 7-4",   time(7, 0),   time(16, 0)),
    ("MOR",  "MOR 7-5",   time(7, 0),   time(17, 0)),

    ("EVE",  "EVE 1-10",  time(13, 0),  time(22, 0)),
    ("EVE",  "EVE 1-11",  time(13, 0),  time(23, 0)),
    ("EVE",  "EVE 2-10",  time(14, 0),  time(22, 0)),
    ("EVE",  "EVE 2-11",  time(14, 0),  time(23, 0)),
    ("EVE",  "EVE 3-10",  time(15, 0),  time(22, 0)),
    ("EVE",  "EVE 3-11",  time(15, 0),  time(23, 0)),
    ("EVE",  "EVE 4-11",  time(16, 0),  time(23, 0)),

    ("NIG",  "NIG 7-4",   time(19, 0),  time(4, 0)),
    ("NIG",  "NIG 8-7",   time(20, 0),  time(7, 0)),
    ("NIG",  "NIG 9-7",   time(21, 0),  time(7, 0)),
    ("NIG",  "NIG 10-7",  time(22, 0),  time(7, 0)),
    ("NIG",  "NIG 11-7",  time(23, 0),  time(7, 0)),

    ("CUST", "Custom",    time(19, 0),  time(4, 0)),

    # ── Leave / off: 1:1 mirrors (no time variants) ──
    # Kept so the roster-cell UI can offer a single dropdown across all
    # ShiftAttributes regardless of category. Drop any line you don't need.
    ("AL",   "AL",        None,         None),
    ("CL",   "CL",        None,         None),
    ("CPL",  "CPL",       None,         None),
    ("LWP",  "LWP",       None,         None),
    ("MTL",  "MTL",       None,         None),
    ("SL",   "SL",        None,         None),
    ("OFF",  "OFF",       None,         None),
]


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Seed ShiftAttribute rows by ShiftType name. Idempotent."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run",
            action="store_true",
            help="Preview without writing.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        dry = opts["dry_run"]

        # Cache ShiftTypes by name (case-insensitive lookup, exact-stored).
        shift_types = {st.name.upper(): st for st in ShiftType.objects.all()}

        created = matched = missing_parent = 0
        rows_to_create: list[ShiftAttribute] = []

        for parent_name, attr_name, start, end in SEED:
            parent = shift_types.get(parent_name.upper())
            if parent is None:
                self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                    f"  skip   {attr_name:12s} — ShiftType {parent_name!r} not found"
                ))
                missing_parent += 1
                continue

            existing = ShiftAttribute.objects.filter(
                shift_type=parent, name=attr_name,
            ).first()
            if existing:
                self.stdout.write(
                    f"  exists {attr_name:12s} → {parent.name}  (pk={existing.pk})"
                )
                matched += 1
                continue

            self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
                f"  create {attr_name:12s} → {parent.name}"
                + (f"  ({start}–{end})" if start and end else "")
            ))
            rows_to_create.append(ShiftAttribute(
                shift_type=parent,
                name=attr_name,
                start_time=start,
                end_time=end,
            ))
            created += 1

        if dry:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                f"\n--dry-run: would create {created}, "
                f"matched {matched}, missing {missing_parent}. Nothing written."
            ))
            return

        if rows_to_create:
            with transaction.atomic():
                # Save one-by-one so ShiftAttribute.save() runs the
                # has_attribute sync on each parent ShiftType.
                for row in rows_to_create:
                    row.save()

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f"\nDone. {created} created, {matched} already existed, "
            f"{missing_parent} skipped (parent ShiftType missing)."
        ))


# ==========================================
# FILE: ./roster/management/commands/delete_shift_types.py
# ==========================================
"""Cascade-delete ShiftType rows along with everything that points to them.

Django admin refuses to delete a ShiftType when there are PROTECT-bound
dependents (Roster patterns, Shifts, LeaveBalances, LeaveApplications,
EncashmentRequests). This command removes the ShiftTypes plus *every*
dependent in the correct order, so a stale set of seeded "test" ShiftTypes
can be wiped out without hand-typing 6 separate deletes in `manage.py shell`.

Usage::

    # Preview what gets deleted, no DB writes
    manage.py delete_shift_types "Morning" "Weekly Off" --dry-run

    # Actually wipe them
    manage.py delete_shift_types "Morning" "Weekly Off" "Casual Leave"

Because this is destructive, the command refuses to run without `--yes` once
you're past the dry-run preview — you have to opt in explicitly.

Cascade order (each step removes the PROTECT block that prevents the next):

    1. LeaveBalanceTransactions tied to balances of these ShiftTypes' policies
    2. EncashmentRequests on those policies
    3. LeaveBalances on those policies
    4. LeaveApplications whose `leave_type` is one of these ShiftTypes
    5. Shifts using these ShiftTypes
    6. Roster pattern rows using these ShiftTypes
    7. The ShiftTypes themselves (LeavePolicy + ShiftAttribute cascade
       automatically — both are CASCADE on ShiftType deletion)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.db import transaction

from leave.models import (
    EncashmentRequest,
    LeaveApplication,
    LeaveBalance,
    LeaveBalanceTransaction,
    LeavePolicy,
)
from roster.models import Roster, Shift, ShiftType


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Cascade-delete ShiftType rows along with all PROTECT-bound dependents."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "names",
            nargs="+",
            help='One or more ShiftType names to delete (case-sensitive). '
                 'Wrap in quotes if the name contains spaces.',
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run",
            action="store_true",
            help="Show counts; don't write anything.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--yes",
            action="store_true",
            help="Required for non-dry-run: confirms you intend to delete data.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        names = opts["names"]
        dry = opts["dry_run"]
        confirmed = opts["yes"]

        targets = ShiftType.objects.filter(name__in=names)
        found = set(targets.values_list("name", flat=True))
        missing = set(names) - found
        if missing:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                f"Not found (skipped): {', '.join(sorted(missing))}"
            ))

        if not targets.exists():
            raise CommandError("No matching ShiftTypes — nothing to do.")

        self.stdout.write(self.style.MIGRATE_HEADING(
            f"\nTargeting {targets.count()} ShiftType(s):"
        ))
        for st in targets.order_by("name"):
            self.stdout.write(f"  · {st.name}  (category={st.category}, pk={st.pk})")

        # Build the dependency querysets up front. Done as querysets (not
        # materialized lists) so the counts are accurate at delete time too.
        policies = LeavePolicy.objects.filter(shift_type__in=targets)
        balances = LeaveBalance.objects.filter(leave_policy__in=policies)
        txns = LeaveBalanceTransaction.objects.filter(balance__in=balances)
        encashments = EncashmentRequest.objects.filter(leave_policy__in=policies)
        applications = LeaveApplication.objects.filter(leave_type__in=targets)
        shifts = Shift.objects.filter(shift_type__in=targets)
        rosters = Roster.objects.filter(shift_type__in=targets)

        self.stdout.write("\nDependents to be deleted:")
        rows = [
            ("LeaveBalanceTransactions", txns.count()),
            ("EncashmentRequests",       encashments.count()),
            ("LeaveBalances",            balances.count()),
            ("LeaveApplications",        applications.count()),
            ("Shifts",                   shifts.count()),
            ("Roster pattern rows",      rosters.count()),
            ("LeavePolicies (cascade)",  policies.count()),
            ("ShiftTypes (target)",      targets.count()),
        ]
        for label, n in rows:
            self.stdout.write(f"  {label:30s} {n}")

        if dry:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                "\n--dry-run: nothing written."
            ))
            return

        if not confirmed:
            raise CommandError(
                "Refusing to delete without --yes. Pass --yes once you've "
                "reviewed the dry-run counts above."
            )

        with transaction.atomic():
            txns.delete()
            encashments.delete()
            balances.delete()
            applications.delete()
            shifts.delete()
            rosters.delete()
            # ShiftType.delete() cascades to LeavePolicy and ShiftAttribute.
            count, _ = targets.delete()

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f"\nDeleted {count} ShiftType(s) and all dependents."
        ))


# ==========================================
# FILE: ./roster/management/commands/fix_shift_attribute_parents.py
# ==========================================
"""Detect and fix ShiftAttributes whose parent ShiftType doesn't match their name.

A ShiftAttribute named ``MOR 8-5`` should belong to the ``MOR`` ShiftType.
If somebody created it under ``EVE`` by mistake (admin UI, a typo, whatever),
every Shift / Roster picking that attribute via the cell-update view stores
``shift_type=EVE`` — which silently ruins the daily / per-row counts on the
roster grid even though the cell still *renders* as "MOR 8-5".

This command:

1. Walks every ShiftAttribute with a non-blank name.
2. Splits the name on whitespace; the first token (case-insensitive) should
   match the parent ShiftType's name.
3. Reports any mismatch. With ``--yes``, reparents the attribute to the
   correct ShiftType (matched by name) and re-saves every Shift / Roster
   row that referenced it — the existing ``Shift.save`` / ``Roster.save``
   override automatically copies ``shift_attribute.shift_type`` onto
   ``self.shift_type``, so the broken classification is fixed in one shot.

Idempotent: a clean DB shows "0 mismatches found." Safe to re-run after
each manual edit.

Usage::

    manage.py fix_shift_attribute_parents --dry-run
    manage.py fix_shift_attribute_parents --yes
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.db import transaction

from roster.models import Roster, Shift, ShiftAttribute, ShiftType


def _expected_parent_name(attr_name: str) -> str | None:
    """First whitespace-delimited token of the attribute name, uppercased.

    ``"MOR 8-5"`` → ``"MOR"``. Returns None for empty / whitespace-only.
    """
    if not attr_name:
        return None
    head = attr_name.strip().split()
    if not head:
        return None
    return head[0].upper()


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Fix ShiftAttributes whose parent ShiftType doesn't match their name prefix."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run",
            action="store_true",
            help="Report mismatches; don't write anything.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--yes",
            action="store_true",
            help="Required for non-dry-run: confirms you intend to repair the data.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        dry = opts["dry_run"]
        confirmed = opts["yes"]

        # Build a name → ShiftType lookup once.
        types_by_name = {
            st.name.upper(): st
            for st in ShiftType.objects.filter(is_active=True)
        }

        attrs = ShiftAttribute.objects.select_related("shift_type").order_by(
            "shift_type__name", "name",
        )
        mismatches: list[tuple[ShiftAttribute, ShiftType]] = []
        unknown_prefixes: list[ShiftAttribute] = []

        for attr in attrs:
            expected_name = _expected_parent_name(attr.name)
            if not expected_name:
                continue
            expected_st = types_by_name.get(expected_name)
            if expected_st is None:
                # The name prefix doesn't match any known ShiftType — could
                # be intentional (e.g. an attribute named "Custom" under
                # CUST). Report so a human can decide; never auto-fix.
                if attr.shift_type and not (attr.shift_type.name.upper().startswith(expected_name)
                                            or expected_name.startswith(attr.shift_type.name.upper())):
                    unknown_prefixes.append(attr)
                continue
            if attr.shift_type_id != expected_st.pk:
                mismatches.append((attr, expected_st))

        if not mismatches and not unknown_prefixes:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
                "0 mismatches found. ShiftAttribute parents look correct."
            ))
            return

        if mismatches:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.MIGRATE_HEADING(
                f"\n{len(mismatches)} mismatched attribute(s):"
            ))
            for attr, expected in mismatches:
                current = attr.shift_type.name if attr.shift_type else "<none>"
                shift_count = Shift.objects.filter(shift_attribute=attr).count()
                roster_count = Roster.objects.filter(shift_attribute=attr).count()
                self.stdout.write(
                    f"  · {attr.name!r:18s} parent={current!r:8s}  "
                    f"→ should be {expected.name!r:8s}  "
                    f"(used by {shift_count} Shift, {roster_count} Roster row{'s' if roster_count != 1 else ''})"
                )

        if unknown_prefixes:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                f"\n{len(unknown_prefixes)} attribute(s) with an unrecognised "
                f"name prefix (review manually):"
            ))
            for attr in unknown_prefixes:
                self.stdout.write(
                    f"  ? {attr.name!r:18s} parent={attr.shift_type.name!r:8s}"
                )

        if dry:
            self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING("\n--dry-run: nothing written."))
            return

        if not confirmed:
            raise CommandError(
                "Refusing to write changes without --yes. Pass --yes once you "
                "have reviewed the mismatch list above."
            )

        if not mismatches:
            self.stdout.write(
                "No clear mismatches to fix; manual-review items left alone."
            )
            return

        with transaction.atomic():
            shift_resaved = roster_resaved = 0
            for attr, expected in mismatches:
                attr.shift_type = expected
                attr.save(update_fields=["shift_type"])
                # Re-save dependent rows so their `shift_type` field is
                # corrected by the model's save-time override.
                for s in Shift.objects.filter(shift_attribute=attr).select_related("shift_attribute"):
                    s.save()
                    shift_resaved += 1
                for r in Roster.objects.filter(shift_attribute=attr).select_related("shift_attribute"):
                    r.save()
                    roster_resaved += 1

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f"\nFixed {len(mismatches)} attribute(s). "
            f"Re-saved {shift_resaved} Shift and {roster_resaved} Roster row(s)."
        ))

"""Seed canonical ShiftType + ShiftAttribute rows for production.

Data is embedded inline (sourced from the SEBPO export
ShiftType-2026-05-06.csv / ShiftAttribute-2026-05-06.csv). The command is
idempotent — re-running update_or_create-s by stable keys.

Replaces the old fixture pair:
    roster/fixtures/seed_shift_types.json
    roster/fixtures/seed_shift_attributes.json
plus the old ``seed_shift_attributes`` management command.

from django.db import transaction

    ("NIG",  "NIG 10-7", time(22, 0), time(7, 0)),
    ("NIG",  "NIG 11-7", time(23, 0), time(7, 0)),
]


class _DryRun(Exception):
    """Sentinel: rolls back the outer atomic block on --dry-run."""


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Seed canonical ShiftType + ShiftAttribute rows from the production export."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run", action="store_true",
            help="Print what would change without writing anything.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        dry = opts["dry_run"]
        try:
            with transaction.atomic():
                self._seed_types()
                self._seed_attributes()
                if dry:
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING("[dry-run] rolling back"))
                    raise _DryRun()
        except _DryRun:
            return
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS("✅ seed_shifts complete"))

    def _seed_types(self):
        created = updated = 0
        for name, description, category, tz, start, end, color in SHIFT_TYPES:
            _, was_created = ShiftType.objects.update_or_create(
                name=name,
                defaults={
                    "description": description,
                    "category": category,
                    "shift_timezone": tz,
                    "shift_start_time": start,
                    "shift_end_time": end,
                    "color": color,
                    "is_active": True,
                },
            )
            if was_created:
                created += 1
            else:
                updated += 1
        self.stdout.write(
            f"ShiftTypes: {created} created, {updated} updated."
        )

    def _seed_attributes(self):
        type_by_name = {st.name: st for st in ShiftType.objects.all()}
        created = updated = skipped = 0
        for parent_name, attr_name, start, end in SHIFT_ATTRIBUTES:
            parent = type_by_name.get(parent_name)
            if parent is None:
                self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                    f"  skip {attr_name} — parent ShiftType '{parent_name}' missing"
                ))
                skipped += 1
                continue
            _, was_created = ShiftAttribute.objects.update_or_create(
                shift_type=parent,
                name=attr_name,
                defaults={
                    "start_time": start,
                    "end_time": end,
                    "description": "",
                },
            )
            if was_created:
                created += 1
            else:
                updated += 1
        self.stdout.write(
            f"ShiftAttributes: {created} created, {updated} updated, "
            f"{skipped} skipped."
        )

# FILE: ./roster/templatetags/roster_tags.py
# ==========================================
"""Template helpers for the roster grid."""

from __future__ import annotations

from django import template

from accounts.locations import resolve_to_dropdown_choice

register = template.Library()


@register.simple_tag
def resolved_location_choice(shift, employee) -> str:
    """Return the canonical dropdown value (MHK/MBD/RAOWA/WFH) for a cell.

    Order of precedence:
        1. The Shift row's own ``job_location`` / ``work_location``
        2. The employee's ``CustomUser.job_location`` / ``work_location``
        3. Empty string when neither resolves to a tracked office or WFH

    Used by ``_cell.html`` to preselect the right option in the per-cell
    location dropdown — explicit per-day overrides take priority, but a
    blank cell still shows the employee's contractual location.
    """
    if shift is not None:
        own = resolve_to_dropdown_choice(shift.job_location, shift.work_location)
        if own:
            return own
    if employee is not None:
        return resolve_to_dropdown_choice(
            getattr(employee, "job_location", None),
            getattr(employee, "work_location", None),
        )
    return ""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixture setup
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class _Hierarchy(TestCase):
    """Org chart used by every test:

        eng_head (heads Eng dept)
        sr_leader (Senior Leadership; Eng dept member)
        hr_user (HR group)
        admin_user (User Admins group)
        superuser (is_superuser)

        pm  ── tl ── ic1
                  └── ic2
        peer_tl (in Eng but doesn't report to pm)
        outsider (in Marketing dept; no relationship)
    """

    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _make_groups()
        cls.eng = Department.objects.create(name="Engineering")
        cls.mkt = Department.objects.create(name="Marketing")
        cls.designation = Designation.objects.create(name="Engineer")

        # Admin tier
        cls.superuser = User.objects.create_superuser(
            email="root@example.com", username="root",
            password="x", first_name="Root", last_name="X",
        )
        cls.hr_user = _user("hr@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        _join_group(cls.hr_user, "HR")
        cls.admin_user = _user("admins@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        _join_group(cls.admin_user, "User Admins")
        cls.sr_leader = _user("cxo@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        _join_group(cls.sr_leader, "Senior Leadership")

        # Line manager hierarchy in Engineering.
        cls.pm = _user("pm@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        cls.tl = _user("tl@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        cls.ic1 = _user("ic1@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        cls.ic2 = _user("ic2@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        cls.peer_tl = _user("peer-tl@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        cls.outsider = _user("outsider@example.com", department=cls.mkt)

        # Wire reports_to via JobInfo. Order matters — children before parents
        # would fail FK constraint? No: JobInfo.reports_to is a CustomUser FK,
        # not a JobInfo FK. So we can set them in any order.
        from employees.models import JobInfo
        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.tl, reports_to=cls.pm)
        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.ic1, reports_to=cls.tl)
        JobInfo.objects.create(employee=cls.ic2, reports_to=cls.tl)

        # Department head — explicit FK on the dept, fires signal.
        cls.dept_head = _user("eng-head@example.com", department=cls.eng)
        cls.eng.head_of_department = cls.dept_head
        cls.eng.save()

        cls.refresh_users()

    @classmethod
    def refresh_users(cls):
        # Refresh from DB so new group memberships set by signals are visible.
        for attr in (
            "superuser", "hr_user", "admin_user", "sr_leader",
            "pm", "tl", "ic1", "ic2", "peer_tl", "outsider", "dept_head",
        ):
            setattr(cls, attr, User.objects.get(pk=getattr(cls, attr).pk))
