class HierarchyTraversalTests(_Hierarchy):
    def test_downline_includes_self(self):
        self.assertIn(self.ic1.pk, downline_pks(self.ic1))

    def test_downline_walks_one_level(self):
        pks = downline_pks(self.tl)
        self.assertIn(self.tl.pk, pks)
        self.assertIn(self.ic1.pk, pks)
        self.assertIn(self.ic2.pk, pks)

    def test_downline_walks_transitively(self):
        pks = downline_pks(self.pm)
        self.assertIn(self.pm.pk, pks)
        self.assertIn(self.tl.pk, pks)
        self.assertIn(self.ic1.pk, pks)
        self.assertIn(self.ic2.pk, pks)
        # peer_tl is not a report
        self.assertNotIn(self.peer_tl.pk, pks)

    def test_downline_excludes_unrelated_users(self):
        pks = downline_pks(self.tl)
        self.assertNotIn(self.peer_tl.pk, pks)
        self.assertNotIn(self.outsider.pk, pks)
        self.assertNotIn(self.pm.pk, pks)

    def test_headed_dept_employee_pks(self):
        pks = headed_dept_employee_pks(self.dept_head)
        # Every active Eng member is included.
        self.assertIn(self.tl.pk, pks)
        self.assertIn(self.ic1.pk, pks)
        self.assertIn(self.peer_tl.pk, pks)
        # Marketing member excluded.
        self.assertNotIn(self.outsider.pk, pks)

    def test_headed_dept_empty_for_non_head(self):
        self.assertEqual(headed_department_pks(self.tl), set())
        self.assertEqual(headed_dept_employee_pks(self.tl), set())

    def test_has_managed_scope(self):
        self.assertTrue(has_managed_scope(self.hr_user))
        self.assertTrue(has_managed_scope(self.tl))         # has direct reports
        self.assertTrue(has_managed_scope(self.dept_head))  # heads a dept
        self.assertFalse(has_managed_scope(self.ic1))       # IC has no scope

class VisibilityTests(_Hierarchy):
    def test_admin_sees_all_active(self):
        pks = visible_employee_pks(self.hr_user)
        for u in (self.tl, self.ic1, self.outsider, self.peer_tl):
            self.assertIn(u.pk, pks)

    def test_senior_leader_sees_all_active(self):
        pks = visible_employee_pks(self.sr_leader)
        self.assertIn(self.outsider.pk, pks)

    def test_manager_sees_downline_plus_self(self):
        qs = visible_employees(self.tl)
        pks = set(qs.values_list("pk", flat=True))
        self.assertEqual(pks, {self.tl.pk, self.ic1.pk, self.ic2.pk})

    def test_dept_head_sees_full_dept_and_self(self):
        qs = visible_employees(self.dept_head)
        pks = set(qs.values_list("pk", flat=True))
        # Every Eng member appears regardless of reports_to chain.
        for u in (self.pm, self.tl, self.ic1, self.ic2, self.peer_tl, self.dept_head):
            self.assertIn(u.pk, pks)
        self.assertNotIn(self.outsider.pk, pks)

    def test_ic_sees_only_self(self):
        qs = visible_employees(self.ic1)
        pks = set(qs.values_list("pk", flat=True))
        self.assertEqual(pks, {self.ic1.pk})

    def test_can_view_employee_matrix(self):
        # IC sees self only.
        self.assertTrue(can_view_employee(self.ic1, self.ic1))
        self.assertFalse(can_view_employee(self.ic1, self.tl))
        # TL sees IC.
        self.assertTrue(can_view_employee(self.tl, self.ic1))
        self.assertFalse(can_view_employee(self.tl, self.peer_tl))
        # Dept head sees peer-TL who is not in their reports_to chain.
        self.assertTrue(can_view_employee(self.dept_head, self.peer_tl))
        # CXO sees everyone.
        self.assertTrue(can_view_employee(self.sr_leader, self.outsider))

            )

            self.assertTrue(
                can_edit_employee_profile(
                    self.dept_head, self.peer_tl, section=section,
                ),
                msg=section,
            )

        for section in ("Contact", "IdentificationNumber", "Address",
                        "PersonalInfo", "LegalIssue"):
            self.assertTrue(
                can_edit_employee_profile(self.ic1, self.ic1, section=section),
                msg=section,
            )

        self.assertFalse(
            can_edit_employee_profile(self.ic1, self.ic1, section="JobInfo")

            can_edit_employee_profile(self.sr_leader, self.ic1, section="Contact")
        )
        self.assertFalse(
            can_edit_employee_profile(self.sr_leader, self.outsider, section="JobInfo")
        )

    def test_stranger_gets_none(self):
        slugs = editable_section_slugs(self.outsider, self.ic1, self.sections)
        self.assertEqual(slugs, set())

class LeaveActionTests(_Hierarchy):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        super().setUpTestData()

        # Make a LEAVE-category ShiftType + a pending application from ic1.
        from roster.models import ShiftType
        from leave.models import LeaveApplication

        # Reuse the seeded LEAVE-category ShiftType when running against
        # MySQL (where the seed migration ran). Fall back to creation
        # under SQLite test settings, which disable migration replay.
        cls.casual, _ = ShiftType.objects.get_or_create(
            name="Casual Leave",
            defaults={
                "category": ShiftType.Category.LEAVE,
                "is_working_shift": False,
                "is_active": True,
            },
        )
        cls.app = LeaveApplication.objects.create(
            employee=cls.ic1,
            leave_type=cls.casual,
            start_date=date(2026, 5, 1),
            end_date=date(2026, 5, 1),
            applied_by=cls.ic1,
        )

    def test_manager_can_act_on_downline_pending(self):
        self.assertTrue(can_act_on_leave(self.tl, self.app))

    def test_dept_head_can_act_on_dept_pending(self):
        self.assertTrue(can_act_on_leave(self.dept_head, self.app))

    def test_admin_can_act(self):
        self.assertTrue(can_act_on_leave(self.hr_user, self.app))

    def test_senior_leadership_cannot_act(self):
        # Read-only.
        self.assertFalse(can_act_on_leave(self.sr_leader, self.app))

    def test_applicant_cannot_approve_own(self):
        self.assertFalse(can_act_on_leave(self.ic1, self.app))

    def test_peer_tl_cannot_act(self):
        self.assertFalse(can_act_on_leave(self.peer_tl, self.app))

    def test_self_cancel_pending(self):
        self.assertTrue(can_cancel_leave(self.ic1, self.app))

    def test_self_cancel_disallowed_after_approval(self):
        self.app.status = self.app.Status.APPROVED
        self.app.save()
        # Applicant alone, non-pending → can no longer self-cancel.
        self.assertFalse(can_cancel_leave(self.ic1, self.app))
        # Manager still can.
        self.assertTrue(can_cancel_leave(self.tl, self.app))

    def test_can_apply_leave_for_self(self):
        self.assertTrue(can_apply_leave_for(self.ic1, self.ic1))

    def test_manager_can_apply_for_downline(self):
        self.assertTrue(can_apply_leave_for(self.tl, self.ic1))

    def test_stranger_cannot_apply_for_others(self):
        self.assertFalse(can_apply_leave_for(self.peer_tl, self.ic1))
        self.assertFalse(can_apply_leave_for(self.outsider, self.ic1))

# Auto-membership signals
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class LineManagerSignalTests(TestCase):
    """The signal adds/removes Line Managers as JobInfo.reports_to changes."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _make_groups()

    def setUp(self):
        from employees.models import JobInfo
        self.JobInfo = JobInfo
        self.alice = _user("alice@example.com")
        self.bob = _user("bob@example.com")
        self.carol = _user("carol@example.com")
        self.line_managers = Group.objects.get(name="Line Managers")

    def _refresh(self, user):
        return User.objects.get(pk=user.pk)

    def test_set_reports_to_adds_manager_to_group(self):
        self.JobInfo.objects.create(employee=self.bob, reports_to=self.alice)
        self.assertTrue(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.line_managers.pk).exists()
        )

    def test_clearing_reports_to_removes_lone_manager(self):
        ji = self.JobInfo.objects.create(employee=self.bob, reports_to=self.alice)
        self.assertTrue(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.line_managers.pk).exists()
        )
        ji.reports_to = None
        ji.save()
        self.assertFalse(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.line_managers.pk).exists()
        )

    def test_changing_manager_swaps_membership(self):
        ji = self.JobInfo.objects.create(employee=self.bob, reports_to=self.alice)
        ji.reports_to = self.carol
        ji.save()
        self.assertFalse(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.line_managers.pk).exists()
        )
        self.assertTrue(
            self._refresh(self.carol).groups.filter(pk=self.line_managers.pk).exists()
        )

    def test_manager_with_two_reports_keeps_membership_when_one_leaves(self):
        ji1 = self.JobInfo.objects.create(employee=self.bob, reports_to=self.alice)
        self.JobInfo.objects.create(employee=self.carol, reports_to=self.alice)
        ji1.reports_to = None
        ji1.save()
        # Alice still manages Carol → still in Line Managers.
        self.assertTrue(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.line_managers.pk).exists()
        )


class DepartmentHeadSignalTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        _make_groups()

    def setUp(self):
        self.eng = Department.objects.create(name="Engineering")
        self.mkt = Department.objects.create(name="Marketing")
        self.alice = _user("alice@example.com")
        self.bob = _user("bob@example.com")
        self.heads = Group.objects.get(name="Department Heads")

    def _refresh(self, user):
        return User.objects.get(pk=user.pk)

    def test_setting_head_adds_to_group(self):
        self.eng.head_of_department = self.alice
        self.eng.save()
        self.assertTrue(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.heads.pk).exists()
        )

    def test_changing_head_removes_old_adds_new(self):
        self.eng.head_of_department = self.alice
        self.eng.save()
        self.eng.head_of_department = self.bob
        self.eng.save()
        self.assertFalse(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.heads.pk).exists()
        )
        self.assertTrue(
            self._refresh(self.bob).groups.filter(pk=self.heads.pk).exists()
        )

    def test_head_of_two_depts_keeps_membership(self):
        self.eng.head_of_department = self.alice
        self.eng.save()
        self.mkt.head_of_department = self.alice
        self.mkt.save()
        self.eng.head_of_department = None
        self.eng.save()
        # Still heads marketing → still in group.
        self.assertTrue(
            self._refresh(self.alice).groups.filter(pk=self.heads.pk).exists()
        )

import uuid

from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser
from django.db import models
from django.utils import timezone

from accounts.managers import CustomUserManager


class _Named(models.Model):
    """Abstract parent for simple reference tables used by org structure."""

    name = models.CharField(max_length=150, unique=True)
    description = models.CharField(max_length=300, blank=True)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(default=timezone.now)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        abstract = True
        ordering = ["name"]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.name


class Department(_Named):
    head_of_department = models.ForeignKey(
        "accounts.CustomUser",
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True,
        blank=True,
        related_name="heads_departments",
        help_text=(
            "Sees and edits everyone in this department, regardless of "
            "the reports-to chain. Used as a backstop when manager links "
            "are missing or out of date."
        ),
    )


class Designation(_Named):
    pass


class AccessLevel(_Named):
    rank = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0, help_text="Higher rank = more senior.")

    class Meta(_Named.Meta):
        ordering = ["-rank", "name"]


class JobLocation(_Named):
    """Where the employee is contractually assigned (e.g. DHK-MHK, DHK-GSN)."""

    code = models.CharField(max_length=20, blank=True)


class WorkLocation(_Named):
    """Where the employee is actually working (WFO, WFH, hybrid)."""


class Team(_Named):
    department = models.ForeignKey(
        Department,
        on_delete=models.PROTECT,
        related_name="teams",
        null=True,
        blank=True,
    )


class SubTeam(_Named):
    team = models.ForeignKey(
        Team,
        on_delete=models.PROTECT,
        related_name="subteams",
    )

    class Meta(_Named.Meta):
        unique_together = [("team", "name")]


class CustomUser(AbstractUser):
    id = models.UUIDField(primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4, editable=False)

    email = models.EmailField(unique=True)
    employee_id = models.CharField(max_length=50, unique=True, null=True, blank=True)

    department = models.ForeignKey(
        Department, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="members"
    )
    designation = models.ForeignKey(
        Designation, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="members"
    )
    access_level = models.ForeignKey(
        AccessLevel, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="members"
    )
    team = models.ForeignKey(
        Team, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="members"
    )
    subteam = models.ForeignKey(
        SubTeam, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="members"
    )
    job_location = models.ForeignKey(
        JobLocation, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="members"
    )
    work_location = models.ForeignKey(
        WorkLocation, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True, related_name="members"
    )

    # Employment lifecycle (ported from ttms, trimmed to actually-used fields).
    joining_date = models.DateField(null=True, blank=True)
    probation_month = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    confirmation_date = models.DateField(null=True, blank=True)
    last_working_date = models.DateField(null=True, blank=True)

    timezone_name = models.CharField(max_length=64, blank=True, default="")
    shift_start_hour = models.DecimalField(
        max_digits=4, decimal_places=2, null=True, blank=True,
        help_text="Default shift start time as decimal hours, e.g. 9.5 for 09:30.",
    )

    signature = models.ImageField(upload_to="signatures/", null=True, blank=True)
    profile_picture = models.ImageField(upload_to="profile_pictures/", null=True, blank=True)
    contact_number = models.CharField(max_length=30, blank=True)

    USERNAME_FIELD = "email"
    REQUIRED_FIELDS = ["username", "first_name", "last_name"]

    objects = CustomUserManager()

    class Meta:
        verbose_name = "Employee"
        verbose_name_plural = "Employees"
        ordering = ["first_name", "last_name"]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.get_full_name() or self.email

    @property
    def display_name(self) -> str:
        return self.get_full_name() or self.username or self.email

# FILE: ./accounts/managers.py
# ==========================================
from django.contrib.auth.base_user import BaseUserManager


class CustomUserManager(BaseUserManager):
    """Manager for the email-as-username CustomUser."""

    use_in_migrations = True

    def _create_user(self, email, username, password, **extra_fields):
        if not email:
            raise ValueError("The email must be set.")
        if not username:
            raise ValueError("The username must be set.")
        email = self.normalize_email(email)
        user = self.model(email=email, username=username, **extra_fields)
        user.set_password(password)
        user.save(using=self._db)
        return user

    def create_user(self, email, username, password=None, **extra_fields):
        extra_fields.setdefault("is_staff", False)
        extra_fields.setdefault("is_superuser", False)
        return self._create_user(email, username, password, **extra_fields)

    def create_superuser(self, email, username, password=None, **extra_fields):
        extra_fields.setdefault("is_staff", True)
        extra_fields.setdefault("is_superuser", True)
        extra_fields.setdefault("is_active", True)
        if extra_fields.get("is_staff") is not True:
            raise ValueError("Superuser must have is_staff=True.")
        if extra_fields.get("is_superuser") is not True:
            raise ValueError("Superuser must have is_superuser=True.")
        return self._create_user(email, username, password, **extra_fields)


# ==========================================
# FILE: ./accounts/locations.py
# ==========================================
"""Canonical office buckets for SEBPO's Dhaka offices.

Azure AD's ``officeLocation`` arrives as free-text and the SSO sync at
``accounts/auth_backends.py`` writes the raw value straight into
``JobLocation.name``. We bucket each ``JobLocation`` into one of three short
codes — ``MBD``, ``MHK``, ``RAOWA`` — by substring match. Anything that
doesn't match (e.g. Chattogram, Gulshan) goes into ``OTHER``. Employees with
no ``job_location`` go into ``UNKNOWN``.

Match order is significant: RAOWA Complex addresses contain "Mohakhali",
so RAOWA is checked before MHK.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

OFFICE_CODES = ("MBD", "MHK", "RAOWA")

_PATTERNS = (
    ("RAOWA", re.compile(r"\bRAOWA\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
    ("MBD",   re.compile(r"\bMBD\b|Monem|Business\s+District", re.IGNORECASE)),
    ("MHK",   re.compile(r"\bMHK\b|Mohakhali|Abbas\s+Garden|\b1206\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
)


def office_bucket(job_location) -> str:
    """Return one of ``MBD`` / ``MHK`` / ``RAOWA`` / ``OTHER`` / ``UNKNOWN``.

    Accepts a ``JobLocation`` instance, a raw string, or ``None``.
    """
    if job_location is None:
        return "UNKNOWN"
    if hasattr(job_location, "name"):
        haystack = " ".join(filter(None, [
            job_location.name or "",
            getattr(job_location, "description", "") or "",
        ]))
    else:
        haystack = str(job_location)
    if not haystack.strip():
        return "UNKNOWN"
    for code, pattern in _PATTERNS:
        if pattern.search(haystack):
            return code
    return "OTHER"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Canonical row resolution for the per-day roster cell location dropdown.
# Surfaces a stable (MBD / MHK / RAOWA / WFH) choice — backed by real
# JobLocation / WorkLocation rows that we get-or-create on first use.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

LOCATION_DROPDOWN_CHOICES = (
    ("MHK",   "MHK"),
    ("MBD",   "MBD"),
    ("RAOWA", "RAOWA"),
    ("WFH",   "WFH"),
)
LOCATION_DROPDOWN_VALUES = {c for c, _ in LOCATION_DROPDOWN_CHOICES}


def get_canonical_office_jobloc(code: str):
    """Return (or create) the canonical ``JobLocation`` for an office code.

    ``code`` is one of ``MBD`` / ``MHK`` / ``RAOWA``. If an existing active
    row already buckets to that code (handles the messy Azure-AD raw
    addresses), we reuse it. Otherwise we create a minimal canonical row
    named after the code so the FK target always exists.
    """
    if code not in OFFICE_CODES:
        return None
    from accounts.models import JobLocation
    # First pass: any existing active row that buckets to this code.
    for jl in JobLocation.objects.filter(is_active=True):
        if office_bucket(jl) == code:
            return jl
    # Fallback: create canonical placeholder. SSO can later auto-create the
    # rich Azure-AD address row; both will continue to bucket to the same code.
    jl, _ = JobLocation.objects.get_or_create(
        name=code, defaults={"code": code, "is_active": True},
    )
    if not jl.code:
        jl.code = code
        jl.save(update_fields=["code"])
    return jl


def get_wfh_worklocation():
    """Return (or create) the WFH ``WorkLocation``."""
    from accounts.models import WorkLocation
    wl = WorkLocation.objects.filter(is_active=True, name__icontains="home").first()
    if wl:
        return wl
    wl, _ = WorkLocation.objects.get_or_create(
        name="Work from Home (WFH)", defaults={"is_active": True},
    )
    return wl


def get_wfo_worklocation():
    """Return (or create) the WFO ``WorkLocation`` (for office days)."""
    from accounts.models import WorkLocation
    wl = WorkLocation.objects.filter(is_active=True, name__icontains="office").first()
    if wl:
        return wl
    wl, _ = WorkLocation.objects.get_or_create(
        name="Work from Office (WFO)", defaults={"is_active": True},
    )
    return wl


def resolve_location_choice(choice: str):
    """Map a dropdown choice (``MHK`` / ``MBD`` / ``RAOWA`` / ``WFH``) to
    a ``(job_location, work_location)`` tuple suitable for assigning to
    a ``Roster`` or ``Shift`` row.

    Empty / unknown choice returns ``(None, None)`` — caller should treat
    that as "leave both unset" so the cell falls back to inherited values.
    """
    if not choice:
        return None, None
    if choice == "WFH":
        return None, get_wfh_worklocation()
    if choice in OFFICE_CODES:
        return get_canonical_office_jobloc(choice), get_wfo_worklocation()
    return None, None


def resolve_to_dropdown_choice(job_location, work_location) -> str:
    """Inverse of ``resolve_location_choice``: collapse a (job, work) pair
    into one of the four dropdown values, or empty if neither matches.
    Falls back to ``office_bucket`` so the canonical short code always wins.
    """
    if work_location:
        up = (work_location.name or "").upper()
        if up.startswith("WORK FROM HOME") or up == "WFH":
            return "WFH"
    if job_location:
        bucket = office_bucket(job_location)
        if bucket in OFFICE_CODES:
            return bucket
    return ""


# ==========================================
# FILE: ./accounts/signals.py
# ==========================================
"""Signal receivers for the accounts app.

Keeps auto-derived group membership in sync as the org structure changes:

- `All Employees`: every active user (created on save).
- `Line Managers`: anyone who is `reports_to` for at least one active
  employee. Recomputed on JobInfo save/delete and CustomUser is_active flip.
- `Department Heads`: whoever is set as `Department.head_of_department`.
  Recomputed on Department save.

Hooked up via `AccountsConfig.ready()`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group
from django.db.models.signals import post_delete, post_save, pre_save
from django.dispatch import receiver


ALL_EMPLOYEES_GROUP = "All Employees"
LINE_MANAGERS_GROUP = "Line Managers"
DEPARTMENT_HEADS_GROUP = "Department Heads"


# --- All Employees --------------------------------------------------------

@receiver(post_save, sender="accounts.CustomUser")
def add_to_all_employees_group(sender, instance, created, **kwargs):
    """Every new user lands in the `All Employees` group.

    Used by dynamic_menu to show company-wide entries (Leave, Dashboard, …)
    without per-user permission management.
    """
    if not created:
        return
    try:
        group = Group.objects.get(name=ALL_EMPLOYEES_GROUP)
    except Group.DoesNotExist:
        return
    instance.groups.add(group)


# --- Line Managers --------------------------------------------------------

@receiver(pre_save, sender="employees.JobInfo")
def stash_previous_reports_to(sender, instance, **kwargs):
    """Stash the prior reports_to_id on the instance so post_save can
    decrement the old manager's Line Managers membership when it changes.

    Cheaper than a model-utils FieldTracker dependency and just as reliable.
    """
    if not instance.pk:
        instance._previous_reports_to_id = None
        return
    try:
        prev = sender.objects.only("reports_to_id").get(pk=instance.pk)
    except sender.DoesNotExist:
        instance._previous_reports_to_id = None
        return
    instance._previous_reports_to_id = prev.reports_to_id


@receiver(post_save, sender="employees.JobInfo")
def sync_line_managers_on_jobinfo_save(sender, instance, **kwargs):
    """Recompute Line Managers membership for the previous + new manager."""
    candidates = set()
    prev = getattr(instance, "_previous_reports_to_id", None)
    if prev:
        candidates.add(prev)
    if instance.reports_to_id:
        candidates.add(instance.reports_to_id)
    if candidates:
        _refresh_line_managers(sender, candidates)


@receiver(post_delete, sender="employees.JobInfo")
def sync_line_managers_on_jobinfo_delete(sender, instance, **kwargs):
    """When a JobInfo (and so an employee) is removed, the manager may
    no longer be a manager of anyone — re-evaluate."""
    if instance.reports_to_id:
        _refresh_line_managers(sender, {instance.reports_to_id})


@receiver(post_save, sender="accounts.CustomUser")
def sync_line_managers_on_active_flip(sender, instance, created, update_fields, **kwargs):
    """Deactivating an employee reduces their manager's report count, which
    may push the manager out of `Line Managers`. Recompute for that manager.
    """
    if created:
        return
    # We only care when activity status may have changed. `update_fields`
    # is None on full saves; assume worst case and refresh the manager too.
    job_info = getattr(instance, "job_info", None)
    if job_info is None:
        return
    if job_info.reports_to_id:
        # Lazily import to avoid circular at module load.
        from employees.models import JobInfo
        _refresh_line_managers(JobInfo, {job_info.reports_to_id})


def _refresh_line_managers(JobInfoModel, manager_pks: set) -> None:
    """For each manager pk, add or remove the Line Managers group based on
    whether they currently have at least one active direct report.
    """
    if not manager_pks:
        return
    group, _ = Group.objects.get_or_create(name=LINE_MANAGERS_GROUP)

    # Bulk-discover which managers still have active reports.
    has_reports = set(
        JobInfoModel.objects
        .filter(reports_to_id__in=manager_pks, employee__is_active=True)
        .values_list("reports_to_id", flat=True)
        .distinct()
    )

    # Sync membership user-by-user. Set is small (few candidates per save),
    # so the row-by-row admin-level group writes are negligible.
    from accounts.models import CustomUser
    for pk in manager_pks:
        user = CustomUser.objects.filter(pk=pk).first()
        if user is None:
            continue
        if pk in has_reports:
            user.groups.add(group)
        else:
            user.groups.remove(group)


# --- Department Heads -----------------------------------------------------

@receiver(pre_save, sender="accounts.Department")
def stash_previous_department_head(sender, instance, **kwargs):
    if not instance.pk:
        instance._previous_head_of_department_id = None
        return
    try:
        prev = sender.objects.only("head_of_department_id").get(pk=instance.pk)
    except sender.DoesNotExist:
        instance._previous_head_of_department_id = None
        return
    instance._previous_head_of_department_id = prev.head_of_department_id


@receiver(post_save, sender="accounts.Department")
def sync_department_heads_on_save(sender, instance, **kwargs):
    """When `head_of_department` is set/changed/cleared, sync the
    Department Heads group.

    Adds the new head; removes the prior head only if they don't head
    any other department.
    """
    candidates = set()
    prev = getattr(instance, "_previous_head_of_department_id", None)
    if prev:
        candidates.add(prev)
    if instance.head_of_department_id:
        candidates.add(instance.head_of_department_id)
    if candidates:
        _refresh_department_heads(sender, candidates)


@receiver(post_delete, sender="accounts.Department")
def sync_department_heads_on_delete(sender, instance, **kwargs):
    if instance.head_of_department_id:
        _refresh_department_heads(sender, {instance.head_of_department_id})


def _refresh_department_heads(DepartmentModel, user_pks: set) -> None:
    if not user_pks:
        return
    group, _ = Group.objects.get_or_create(name=DEPARTMENT_HEADS_GROUP)

    still_heading = set(
        DepartmentModel.objects
        .filter(head_of_department_id__in=user_pks)
        .values_list("head_of_department_id", flat=True)
        .distinct()
    )

    from accounts.models import CustomUser
    for pk in user_pks:
        user = CustomUser.objects.filter(pk=pk).first()
        if user is None:
            continue
        if pk in still_heading:
            user.groups.add(group)
        else:
            user.groups.remove(group)

from django.contrib import messages
from django.contrib.auth import views as auth_views
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.contrib.auth.mixins import LoginRequiredMixin, UserPassesTestMixin
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render
from django.urls import reverse_lazy
from django.views.generic import CreateView, DeleteView, ListView, UpdateView

from accounts.forms import (
    CustomUserCreationForm,
    CustomUserUpdateForm,
    EmailLoginForm,
)
from accounts.models import CustomUser


class StaffRequiredMixin(LoginRequiredMixin, UserPassesTestMixin):
    """User must be authenticated AND a staff member."""

    def test_func(self):
        user = self.request.user
        return user.is_authenticated and user.is_staff


class OrbisLoginView(auth_views.LoginView):
    template_name = "auth/login.html"
    authentication_form = EmailLoginForm
    redirect_authenticated_user = True

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        # Detect the silent-bounce case: user signed in successfully at Microsoft
        # but Orbis refused them (most often because their CustomUser row doesn't
        # exist yet and OIDC_CREATE_USER is False). They land back here with
        # /oidc/callback/ as the referer — show them why instead of a blank form.
        referer = self.request.META.get("HTTP_REFERER", "")
        ctx["sso_bounce"] = "/oidc/callback/" in referer or "/oidc/" in referer
        return ctx


class OrbisLogoutView(auth_views.LogoutView):
    next_page = reverse_lazy("login")


class UserListView(StaffRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = CustomUser
    template_name = "accounts/user_list.html"
    context_object_name = "users"
    paginate_by = 25
    extra_context = {"page_title": "Users"}

    def get_queryset(self):
        qs = super().get_queryset().select_related("department", "designation", "job_location")
        q = self.request.GET.get("q", "").strip()
        if q:
            qs = qs.filter(email__icontains=q) | qs.filter(first_name__icontains=q) \
                 | qs.filter(last_name__icontains=q) | qs.filter(employee_id__icontains=q)
        return qs.order_by("first_name", "last_name")


class UserCreateView(StaffRequiredMixin, CreateView):
    model = CustomUser
    form_class = CustomUserCreationForm
    template_name = "accounts/user_form.html"
    success_url = reverse_lazy("user_list")

    def form_valid(self, form):
        response = super().form_valid(form)
        messages.success(self.request, f"Created user {self.object.email}.")
        return response

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        ctx["page_title"] = "Create user"
        ctx["submit_label"] = "Create user"
        return ctx


class UserUpdateView(StaffRequiredMixin, UpdateView):
    model = CustomUser
    form_class = CustomUserUpdateForm
    template_name = "accounts/user_form.html"
    success_url = reverse_lazy("user_list")

    def form_valid(self, form):
        response = super().form_valid(form)
        messages.success(self.request, f"Updated user {self.object.email}.")
        return response

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        ctx["page_title"] = f"Edit {self.object.display_name}"
        ctx["submit_label"] = "Save changes"
        return ctx


class UserDeleteView(StaffRequiredMixin, DeleteView):
    model = CustomUser
    template_name = "accounts/user_confirm_delete.html"
    success_url = reverse_lazy("user_list")

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        ctx["page_title"] = f"Delete {self.object.display_name}"
        return ctx

    def form_valid(self, form):
        messages.success(self.request, f"Deleted user {self.object.email}.")
        return super().form_valid(form)

from django import forms
from django.contrib.auth.forms import (
    AuthenticationForm,
    UserCreationForm,
)

from accounts.models import CustomUser
from core.forms import StyledMixin as _StyledMixin


class EmailLoginForm(AuthenticationForm, _StyledMixin):
    """Login by email + password. Overrides the username field label/placeholder."""

    username = forms.EmailField(
        label="Email",
        widget=forms.EmailInput(attrs={"autofocus": True, "autocomplete": "email",
                                        "placeholder": "you@sebpo.net"}),
    )
    password = forms.CharField(
        label="Password",
        widget=forms.PasswordInput(attrs={"autocomplete": "current-password",
                                           "placeholder": "••••••••"}),
    )

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.style_widgets()


class CustomUserCreationForm(UserCreationForm, _StyledMixin):
    class Meta:
        model = CustomUser
        fields = ("email", "username", "first_name", "last_name",
                  "employee_id", "department", "designation",
                  "team", "subteam", "job_location", "work_location",
                  "contact_number", "is_active")

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.style_widgets()


class CustomUserUpdateForm(forms.ModelForm, _StyledMixin):
    class Meta:
        model = CustomUser
        fields = ("email", "username", "first_name", "last_name",
                  "employee_id", "department", "designation", "access_level",
                  "team", "subteam", "job_location", "work_location",
                  "contact_number", "joining_date", "probation_month",
                  "confirmation_date", "last_working_date",
                  "is_active", "groups")

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        for date_field in ("joining_date", "confirmation_date", "last_working_date"):
            self.fields[date_field].widget = forms.DateInput(
                attrs={
                    "type": "text",
                    "placeholder": "YYYY-MM-DD",
                    "data-flatpickr": "",
                    "autocomplete": "off",
                    "pattern": r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}",
                },
                format="%Y-%m-%d",
            )
            self.fields[date_field].input_formats = ["%Y-%m-%d"]
        self.style_widgets()

# ==========================================
# FILE: ./accounts/auth_backends.py
# ==========================================
"""Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) OIDC authentication backend for Orbis.

Subclass of `mozilla_django_oidc.auth.OIDCAuthenticationBackend` that:

- Links Entra identities to existing CustomUser rows by email — does NOT
  auto-create users (admin pre-creates them; OIDC_CREATE_USER=False in settings).
- Enriches the user from Microsoft Graph `/me` on every login: names, employee_id,
  joining_date, department / designation / job_location (auto-provisioned by name),
  contact_number, and JobInfo.reports_to (manager — only when the manager already
  has an Orbis account).
- Falls back gracefully if the Graph call fails — login still completes using
  the id_token claims, just without the rich enrichment.

The Graph $select + $expand=manager(...) query is configured via OIDC_OP_USER_ENDPOINT
in core/settings.py — the parent `get_userinfo` method GETs that URL with the
access token, so we don't need to hand-roll the Graph call.
"""

import base64
import json
import logging
from datetime import date, datetime

import requests
from mozilla_django_oidc.auth import OIDCAuthenticationBackend

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _decode_jwt_payload_unsafe(token: str) -> dict:
    """Base64-decode a JWT's payload segment without verifying signature.

    Used only for diagnostic logging — we trust the token because it came
    from Microsoft over a TLS-validated OIDC flow; we just want to *peek*
    at the `scp` (scopes) and `aud` claims to debug Graph 403s.
    """
    try:
        parts = token.split(".")
        if len(parts) < 2:
            return {}
        payload_b64 = parts[1]
        # Re-pad if base64url stripped trailing `=`s.
        padding = (-len(payload_b64)) % 4
        payload_b64 += "=" * padding
        return json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(payload_b64))
    except Exception:
        return {}


def _email_from_graph(payload: dict) -> str:
    """Graph sometimes returns `mail` as null for guest accounts; fall back to UPN."""
    return (payload.get("mail") or payload.get("userPrincipalName") or "").strip().lower()


def _parse_hire_date(value):
    """Parse Graph's `employeeHireDate` (ISO 8601 string) into a date."""
    if not value:
        return None
    try:
        if "T" in value:
            return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00")).date()
        return date.fromisoformat(value)
    except (ValueError, AttributeError, TypeError):
        return None


class OrbisOIDCBackend(OIDCAuthenticationBackend):

    def get_userinfo(self, access_token, id_token, payload):
        """Call Graph /me with our $select + $expand. On failure, retry without
        the manager $expand (which requires User.Read.All), then fall back to
        the id_token payload as a last resort. This way, login still works and
        basic profile enrichment happens even when User.Read.All isn't
        admin-consented — only the manager auto-link is skipped.
        """
        try:
            return super().get_userinfo(access_token, id_token, payload)
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            # When the call fails, peek at the actual scopes Entra granted —
            # makes diagnosing missing-permission 403s a one-line answer
            # instead of a hours-long round-trip with IT.
            scopes = _decode_jwt_payload_unsafe(access_token).get("scp", "")
            logger.warning(
                "Graph /me with $expand=manager failed (%s); token scopes: %r; "
                "retrying without manager expansion.",
                exc, scopes,
            )

        # Retry without $expand=manager. Drops only the manager field; all
        # other selected fields (employeeId, jobTitle, department, etc.) come
        # back fine with just User.Read.
        try:
            response = requests.get(
                "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me"
                "?$select=id,displayName,givenName,surname,mail,"
                "userPrincipalName,jobTitle,department,officeLocation,"
                "employeeId,employeeHireDate,mobilePhone,companyName",
                headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"},
                timeout=10,
            )
            response.raise_for_status()
            return response.json()
        except requests.RequestException as exc:
            logger.warning(
                "Graph /me without manager also failed (%s); "
                "falling back to id_token claims (sparse enrichment).",
                exc,
            )
            return payload

    def verify_claims(self, claims):
        """Override the default `email`-only check — Graph /me returns `mail`
        / `userPrincipalName`, not `email`. Accept either source."""
        if _email_from_graph(claims) or claims.get("email"):
            return True
        logger.warning(
            "OIDC verify_claims failed — no email in claims. Keys present: %s",
            sorted(claims.keys()) if isinstance(claims, dict) else type(claims).__name__,
        )
        return False

    def filter_users_by_claims(self, claims):
        email = _email_from_graph(claims) or (claims.get("email") or "").strip().lower()
        if not email:
            return self.UserModel.objects.none()
        qs = self.UserModel.objects.filter(email__iexact=email)
        if not qs.exists():
            from django.conf import settings as dj_settings
            if not dj_settings.OIDC_CREATE_USER:
                # Only log a "reject" when auto-create is off and the user
                # is genuinely going to bounce. With full JIT, this is just
                # a first-time login (handled by create_user) — not a reject.
                logger.warning(
                    "OIDC reject (user not provisioned): %s — pre-create with "
                    "`manage.py preprovision_sso_user %s` or set "
                    "OIDC_AUTO_CREATE_USERS=1 to auto-onboard.",
                    email, email,
                )
            else:
                logger.info("OIDC first-time login (will auto-create): %s", email)
        return qs

    def create_user(self, claims):
        """Auto-create a CustomUser from Graph claims on first SSO login.

        Overrides mozilla-django-oidc's default for two reasons:

        1. Default reads `claims['email']`, but Graph's `/me` returns `mail`
           / `userPrincipalName` (not `email`). Email is USERNAME_FIELD on
           CustomUser, so we set both consistently.
        2. **Critically**: mozilla-django-oidc's parent `authenticate` does
           NOT call `update_user` for newly-created users — it returns the
           bare user from `create_user` and stops. Without chaining into
           `update_user` here, first-time SSO sign-ins would never get
           `employee_id`, `department`, `designation`, `job_location`,
           `mobilePhone`, or `manager` populated from Graph; only returning
           users would get the full enrichment. Calling `update_user` from
           within `create_user` makes the first-login profile match what
           subsequent logins produce.
        """
        email = _email_from_graph(claims) or (claims.get("email") or "").strip().lower()
        if not email:
            # Defensive: verify_claims should have caught this already.
            raise ValueError("Cannot create OIDC user without an email claim.")
        user = self.UserModel.objects.create_user(
            email=email,
            username=email[:150],
            first_name=(claims.get("givenName") or claims.get("given_name") or "").strip(),
            last_name=(claims.get("surname") or claims.get("family_name") or "").strip(),
        )
        user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save(update_fields=["password"])
        logger.info("OIDC auto-onboarded new user: %s", email)
        # Chain into update_user so the first-login profile matches what
        # subsequent logins produce (employee_id, jobTitle, dept, etc.).
        return self.update_user(user, claims)

    def update_user(self, user, claims):
        from accounts.models import Department, Designation, JobLocation
        from employees.models import JobInfo

        # Diagnostic: surface which Graph fields actually came back so
        # "nothing populated" reports can be triaged without DB access.
        # Empty `missing` = Graph is fine, Orbis is doing its job.
        # Non-empty `missing` = Entra/Graph sync gap, fix is upstream.
        graph_keys = (
            "employeeId", "jobTitle", "department", "officeLocation",
            "employeeHireDate", "mobilePhone", "manager",
        )
        present = sorted(k for k in graph_keys if claims.get(k))
        missing = sorted(k for k in graph_keys if not claims.get(k))
        logger.info(
            "Graph profile sync for %s: present=%s missing=%s",
            user.email, present, missing,
        )

        # Names (prefer Graph, fall back to id_token claim names if Graph failed).
        user.first_name = (
            claims.get("givenName") or claims.get("given_name") or user.first_name
        )
        user.last_name = (
            claims.get("surname") or claims.get("family_name") or user.last_name
        )

        if claims.get("employeeId"):
            user.employee_id = claims["employeeId"]

        # Hire date is a one-shot enrichment — don't overwrite an admin-set value.
        if not user.joining_date:
            hire_date = _parse_hire_date(claims.get("employeeHireDate"))
            if hire_date:
                user.joining_date = hire_date

        # FK enrichment — auto-provision the reference rows by name. Admin can
        # rename / merge duplicates later.
        dept_name = (claims.get("department") or "").strip()
        if dept_name:
            user.department, _ = Department.objects.get_or_create(name=dept_name)

        title = (claims.get("jobTitle") or "").strip()
        if title:
            user.designation, _ = Designation.objects.get_or_create(name=title)

        office = (claims.get("officeLocation") or "").strip()
        if office:
            user.job_location, _ = JobLocation.objects.get_or_create(name=office)

        if not user.contact_number and claims.get("mobilePhone"):
            user.contact_number = claims["mobilePhone"]

        user.save()

        # Manager → JobInfo.reports_to. If the manager doesn't exist as an Orbis
        # user yet, create a stub so the org chart isn't broken — the stub gets
        # fully enriched the first time that manager themselves signs in via SSO.
        manager_data = claims.get("manager") or {}
        manager_email = _email_from_graph(manager_data)
        if manager_email:
            logger.info(
                "Graph manager for %s: %s (%s)",
                user.email,
                manager_email,
                manager_data.get("displayName") or "(no displayName)",
            )
            manager_user = self._get_or_create_manager(manager_data)
            if manager_user and manager_user.pk != user.pk:
                ji, _ = JobInfo.objects.get_or_create(employee=user)
                if ji.reports_to_id != manager_user.pk:
                    ji.reports_to = manager_user
                    ji.save(update_fields=["reports_to", "updated_at"])
                    logger.info(
                        "Set %s.reports_to → %s",
                        user.email, manager_user.email,
                    )

        return user

    def _get_or_create_manager(self, manager_data):
        """Resolve a manager from Graph's $expand=manager(...) payload.

        Returns the existing CustomUser if one matches by email; otherwise
        creates a minimal stub (email + displayName + jobTitle) with an
        unusable password. The stub becomes a normal user the first time
        that manager signs in via SSO.
        """
        from accounts.models import Designation

        email = _email_from_graph(manager_data)
        if not email:
            return None

        existing = self.UserModel.objects.filter(email__iexact=email).first()
        if existing:
            return existing

        display = (manager_data.get("displayName") or "").strip()
        first_name, _, last_name = display.partition(" ")

        stub = self.UserModel.objects.create_user(
            email=email,
            username=email[:150],
            first_name=first_name,
            last_name=last_name,
        )
        stub.set_unusable_password()

        title = (manager_data.get("jobTitle") or "").strip()
        if title:
            stub.designation, _ = Designation.objects.get_or_create(name=title)

        stub.save()
        logger.info(
            "Created manager stub %s (%s); will be enriched on first SSO login.",
            email, display or "(no displayName)",
        )
        return stub

# ==========================================
# FILE: ./accounts/permissions.py
# ==========================================
"""Centralized permission resolver for Orbis.

Single source of truth for:
- "Who can a user see?" (visibility scope)
- "Who can a user edit?" (write scope)
- "Can this user act on this leave / roster / profile?"

All helpers accept an optional `request` so per-request results memoize on
`request._perm_cache`. Templates rendering N rows pay the DB cost once.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model

from accounts.models import Department


User = get_user_model()


# --- Group definitions ----------------------------------------------------

ADMIN_GROUPS_ALL_VIEW = {"User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership"}
ADMIN_GROUPS_ALL_EDIT = {"User Admins", "HR"}  # Senior Leadership is read-only.

LINE_MANAGERS_GROUP = "Line Managers"
DEPARTMENT_HEADS_GROUP = "Department Heads"
SENIOR_LEADERSHIP_GROUP = "Senior Leadership"

# Sections an employee may edit on their own profile. JobInfo is intentionally
# excluded: department / designation / reports_to / joining_date are HR-managed
# organizational facts, not personal data.
SELF_EDITABLE_SECTIONS = {
    "PersonalInfo", "FamilyInfo", "Contact", "Address", "Email",
    "Education", "Nominee", "Reference", "ProfessionalCertification",
    "Vaccination", "IdentificationNumber", "LegalIssue", "Image",
}


# --- Per-request memoization ----------------------------------------------

def _request_cache(request):
    """Return the per-request memo dict (or None when no request is given).

    Helpers without a request — signals, management commands — bypass the
    cache and compute fresh, which is correct for those non-request paths.
    """
    if request is None:
        return None
    cache = getattr(request, "_perm_cache", None)
    if cache is None:
        cache = {}
        request._perm_cache = cache
    return cache


def _cached(request, key, compute):
    cache = _request_cache(request)
    if cache is not None and key in cache:
        return cache[key]
    value = compute()
    if cache is not None:
        cache[key] = value
    return value


# --- Group membership -----------------------------------------------------

def user_groups(user, request=None) -> set[str]:
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return set()
    return _cached(
        request, ("user_groups", user.pk),
        lambda: set(user.groups.values_list("name", flat=True)),
    )


def can_see_all(user, request=None) -> bool:
    """Org-wide read scope. Superuser + admin/HR/SrLeadership groups."""
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return False
    if user.is_superuser:
        return True
    return bool(user_groups(user, request) & ADMIN_GROUPS_ALL_VIEW)


def can_edit_all(user, request=None) -> bool:
    """Org-wide write scope. Superuser + User Admins + HR.

    Senior Leadership is deliberately excluded — they read everything but
    don't approve leave / edit roster cells / edit profiles. Grant individual
    CXOs `User Admins` membership if they need write access.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return False
    if user.is_superuser:
        return True
    return bool(user_groups(user, request) & ADMIN_GROUPS_ALL_EDIT)


# --- Hierarchy traversal --------------------------------------------------

def _compute_downline_pks(user) -> set:
    """BFS of JobInfo.reports_to subtree, including the user themselves.

    Each iteration is one indexed `IN (frontier)` query against
    `employees_jobinfo.reports_to_id`. Total queries == depth of subtree
    (~5–6 layers at SEBPO scale).
    """
    # Imported here to avoid a circular import: accounts -> employees -> accounts.
    from employees.models import JobInfo

    result = {user.pk}
    frontier = {user.pk}
    while frontier:
        nxt = set(
            JobInfo.objects
            .filter(reports_to_id__in=frontier)
            .values_list("employee_id", flat=True)
        )
        nxt -= result
        if not nxt:
            break
        result |= nxt
        frontier = nxt
    return result


def downline_pks(user, request=None) -> set:
    """User PKs of self + every transitive direct report."""
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return set()
    return _cached(
        request, ("downline", user.pk),
        lambda: _compute_downline_pks(user),
    )


def headed_department_pks(user, request=None) -> set:
    """Department PKs where this user is the explicit head_of_department."""
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return set()
    return _cached(
        request, ("headed_dept", user.pk),
        lambda: set(
            Department.objects
            .filter(head_of_department=user, is_active=True)
            .values_list("pk", flat=True)
        ),
    )


def headed_dept_employee_pks(user, request=None) -> set:
    """User PKs of all members of every department this user heads."""
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return set()
    dept_ids = headed_department_pks(user, request)
    if not dept_ids:
        return set()
    return _cached(
        request, ("headed_dept_emp", user.pk),
        lambda: set(
            User.objects
            .filter(department_id__in=dept_ids, is_active=True)
            .values_list("pk", flat=True)
        ),
    )


def visible_employee_pks(user, request=None) -> set:
    """Union of self + downline + headed-dept members.

    For org-wide viewers this materialises all active employee pks in one
    query — the caller usually doesn't need that, so prefer `visible_employees`
    (a queryset) for list views.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return set()
    if can_see_all(user, request):
        return _cached(
            request, ("all_active_pks",),
            lambda: set(
                User.objects.filter(is_active=True).values_list("pk", flat=True)
            ),
        )
    return (
        downline_pks(user, request)
        | headed_dept_employee_pks(user, request)
        | {user.pk}
    )


def visible_employees(user, request=None):
    """QuerySet form for list views and form widgets."""
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return User.objects.none()
    qs = User.objects.filter(is_active=True)
    if can_see_all(user, request):
        return qs
    return qs.filter(
        pk__in=(
            downline_pks(user, request)
            | headed_dept_employee_pks(user, request)
            | {user.pk}
        )
    )


def has_managed_scope(user, request=None) -> bool:
    """True if the user has anyone in their write scope beyond themselves.

    Cheap signal for sidebar gating ("show Approvals tab"). Distinct from
    `is_in_group("Line Managers")` because dept heads with no direct reports
    still have approvals to do.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return False
    if can_edit_all(user, request):
        return True
    return bool(
        (downline_pks(user, request) - {user.pk})
        | headed_dept_employee_pks(user, request)
    )


# --- Capability checks ----------------------------------------------------

def can_view_employee(user, target, request=None) -> bool:
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated or not target:
        return False
    if can_see_all(user, request):
        return True
    return target.pk in visible_employee_pks(user, request)


def _in_managed_scope(user, target_pk, request=None) -> bool:
    return target_pk in (
        downline_pks(user, request) | headed_dept_employee_pks(user, request)
    )


def can_edit_employee_profile(user, target, section: str | None = None, request=None) -> bool:
    """Edit a section of an employee's profile.

    `section` is the model class name of the section (e.g., "Contact",
    "JobInfo", "IdentificationNumber"). Self-edit is allowed only for
    sections in SELF_EDITABLE_SECTIONS — JobInfo never qualifies.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated or not target:
        return False
    if can_edit_all(user, request):
        return True
    if target.pk == user.pk:
        return section in SELF_EDITABLE_SECTIONS
    return _in_managed_scope(user, target.pk, request)


def editable_section_slugs(user, target, sections, request=None) -> set[str]:
    """Pre-compute the set of editable section slugs for one viewer/target.

    `sections` is an iterable of objects with `.slug` and `.model`; matches
    the SectionSpec shape from `employees.sections`. Returns a set of slugs
    the template can do O(1) `{% if spec.slug in editable_section_slugs %}`
    on.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated or not target:
        return set()
    if can_edit_all(user, request):
        return {s.slug for s in sections}
    if target.pk == user.pk:
        return {
            s.slug for s in sections
            if s.model.__name__ in SELF_EDITABLE_SECTIONS
        }
    if _in_managed_scope(user, target.pk, request):
        return {s.slug for s in sections}
    return set()


def can_edit_roster_pattern(user, target, request=None) -> bool:
    """Edit anyone's weekly pattern or daily cell.

    Same scope as profile edit (admin / manager / dept head), with one
    preserved rule: a non-admin can never edit their own pattern or cells.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated or not target:
        return False
    if can_edit_all(user, request):
        return True
    if target.pk == user.pk:
        return False
    return _in_managed_scope(user, target.pk, request)


def can_act_on_leave(user, application, request=None) -> bool:
    """Approve or decline a leave request.

    Admins (HR / User Admins) can approve anyone, including their own
    requests today (the separation-of-duties tightening is deferred — see
    docs/PLAN.md open items). Non-admins can never approve their own; they
    can approve anyone in their managed scope (downline ∪ headed dept).
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated or not application:
        return False
    if can_edit_all(user, request):
        return True
    if application.employee_id == user.pk:
        return False
    return _in_managed_scope(user, application.employee_id, request)


def can_cancel_leave(user, application, request=None) -> bool:
    """Cancel a leave request.

    Applicant can cancel their own while it's pending; managers / admins
    can cancel any state.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated or not application:
        return False
    if application.employee_id == user.pk and application.is_pending:
        return True
    return can_act_on_leave(user, application, request)


def can_apply_leave_for(user, target, request=None) -> bool:
    """Apply for leave on behalf of another employee.

    Self always allowed; admins always allowed; managers can apply for
    their managed scope.
    """
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated or not target:
        return False
    if target.pk == user.pk:
        return True
    if can_edit_all(user, request):
        return True
    return _in_managed_scope(user, target.pk, request)

# ==========================================
# FILE: ./accounts/management/commands/import_org_chart.py
# ==========================================
"""Import employees + manager hierarchy from a CSV.

Use case: when Microsoft Graph's `User.Read.All` admin consent isn't (yet)
granted for the Orbis app registration, the auto-populated `JobInfo.reports_to`
from `$expand=manager` won't work. This command lets HR push the org chart
from a Workday / Oracle Fusion export instead — zero Azure dependency.

CSV format (headers required, columns ordered any way):

    email,manager_email,first_name,last_name,employee_id
    alice@sebpo.com,bob@sebpo.com,Alice,Rahman,E1001
    charlie@sebpo.com,bob@sebpo.com,Charlie,Khan,E1002
    bob@sebpo.com,,Bob,Hossain,E1003

Required columns: ``email``.
Optional columns: ``manager_email`` (if present and non-empty, sets
``JobInfo.reports_to``), ``first_name``, ``last_name``, ``employee_id``.

Behaviour:

- Each row's user is created if missing (same JIT pattern as SSO sign-in).
- Each manager referenced is also created if missing (stub with unusable
  password — gets enriched when they themselves first sign in via SSO).
- Optional fields are written only when the CSV column is non-empty —
  never overwrites with blanks.
- Reports against itself: if a row's manager_email == email, that row is
  skipped with a warning (no self-reporting allowed).
- Use ``--dry-run`` to preview without touching the database.

Usage::

    manage.py import_org_chart /tmp/orbis_org.csv
    manage.py import_org_chart /tmp/orbis_org.csv --dry-run
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
from pathlib import Path

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from django.db import transaction

from accounts.models import CustomUser
from employees.models import JobInfo


REQUIRED_COLUMNS = {"email"}
OPTIONAL_COLUMNS = {"manager_email", "first_name", "last_name", "employee_id"}


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Import org chart (users + reports_to) from a CSV."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument("csv_path", help="Path to the CSV file.")
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run",
            action="store_true",
            help="Parse and validate the CSV; print what would change without writing.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        path = Path(opts["csv_path"])
        if not path.is_file():
            raise CommandError(f"File not found: {path}")

        with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
            reader = csv.DictReader(f)
            if not reader.fieldnames:
                raise CommandError(f"{path} has no header row.")
            cols = {c.strip().lower() for c in reader.fieldnames}
            missing = REQUIRED_COLUMNS - cols
            if missing:
                raise CommandError(
                    f"CSV missing required column(s): {', '.join(sorted(missing))}. "
                    f"Got: {', '.join(reader.fieldnames)}"
                )
            unknown = cols - REQUIRED_COLUMNS - OPTIONAL_COLUMNS
            if unknown:
                self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                    f"Ignoring unknown column(s): {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}"
                ))
            rows = [
                {(k or "").strip().lower(): (v or "").strip() for k, v in row.items()}
                for row in reader
            ]

        if not rows:
            raise CommandError(f"{path} contained no data rows.")

        dry = opts["dry_run"]
        self.stdout.write(
            f"Parsed {len(rows)} row(s) from {path}"
            + (" (DRY RUN — no DB writes)" if dry else "")
        )
        self.stdout.write("")

        created_users = updated_users = linked_managers = 0
        skipped_self_report = 0

        with transaction.atomic():
            for i, row in enumerate(rows, start=2):  # row 1 is the header
                email = row.get("email", "").lower()
                if not email:
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                        f"  row {i}: missing email — skipped"
                    ))
                    continue

                manager_email = row.get("manager_email", "").lower()
                if manager_email == email:
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                        f"  row {i}: {email} reports to itself — skipped"
                    ))
                    skipped_self_report += 1
                    continue

                user, was_created = self._upsert_user(
                    email=email,
                    first_name=row.get("first_name", ""),
                    last_name=row.get("last_name", ""),
                    employee_id=row.get("employee_id", ""),
                    dry=dry,
                )
                if was_created:
                    created_users += 1
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
                        f"  row {i}: created  {email}"
                    ))
                else:
                    updated_users += 1

                if manager_email:
                    manager, manager_created = self._upsert_user(
                        email=manager_email, dry=dry,
                    )
                    if manager_created:
                        created_users += 1
                        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
                            f"           created stub for manager  {manager_email}"
                        ))
                    if not dry and user is not None and manager is not None:
                        ji, _ = JobInfo.objects.get_or_create(employee=user)
                        if ji.reports_to_id != manager.pk:
                            ji.reports_to = manager
                            ji.save(update_fields=["reports_to", "updated_at"])
                            linked_managers += 1
                    elif dry and email != manager_email:
                        # Just report what we'd do
                        linked_managers += 1
                        self.stdout.write(
                            f"           would link  {email} → {manager_email}"
                        )

            if dry:
                # Roll back any read-only side effects (shouldn't be any, but
                # safer to be explicit).
                transaction.set_rollback(True)

        self.stdout.write("")
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(
            f"Done. {created_users} created · {updated_users} matched · "
            f"{linked_managers} reports_to links · {skipped_self_report} skipped"
            + (" (rolled back; nothing written)" if dry else "")
        ))

    def _upsert_user(self, *, email, first_name="", last_name="", employee_id="", dry=False):
        """Get-or-create a user; optionally update name / employee_id when given.

        Returns (user_or_None_in_dry_run_create_path, was_created_bool).
        """
        existing = CustomUser.objects.filter(email__iexact=email).first()
        if existing:
            updated_fields = []
            if first_name and existing.first_name != first_name:
                existing.first_name = first_name
                updated_fields.append("first_name")
            if last_name and existing.last_name != last_name:
                existing.last_name = last_name
                updated_fields.append("last_name")
            if employee_id and existing.employee_id != employee_id:
                existing.employee_id = employee_id
                updated_fields.append("employee_id")
            if updated_fields and not dry:
                existing.save(update_fields=updated_fields)
            return existing, False

        if dry:
            return None, True

        user = CustomUser.objects.create_user(
            email=email,
            username=email[:150],
            first_name=first_name or "",
            last_name=last_name or "",
        )
        if employee_id:
            user.employee_id = employee_id
        user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        return user, True


# ==========================================
# FILE: ./accounts/management/commands/seed_orbis.py
# ==========================================
"""Idempotent orchestrator for first-run / re-seedable Orbis data.

Wraps every initial-population step in one transactional command. Safe to
re-run: groups, menus, JobLocations are ``get_or_create``-d by stable keys,
fixtures use explicit pks (`loaddata` is upsert-by-pk), and the per-app
``seed_*`` commands are themselves idempotent.

Replaces the seeding work previously split across the deploy script's
multi-loaddata loop **plus** the data migrations
(``accounts/0003_seed_hierarchy_groups`` and
``leave/0002_all_employees_group_and_menu``) that were dropped during the
production migration squash.

Order matters — fixtures depend on groups (e.g. menu rows reference auth
groups by pk), and ``seed_leave_policies`` depends on the seeded ShiftTypes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django.db import transaction


# Stable ordering: groups Orbis relies on. Re-running creates nothing new.
ORBIS_GROUPS = (
    "User Admins",
    "HR",
    "Roster Planner",
    "All Employees",
    "Line Managers",
    "Senior Leadership",
    "Department Heads",
    # Clearance teams for the offboarding workflow.
    "IT",
    "Finance",
    "Admin Facilities",
    "HR Head",
)

# Each entry: ``(title, icon_class, route_name, rank, [group_names])``.
# `route_name` must match a `name=...` in the corresponding app's `urls.py`.
ORBIS_MAIN_MENUS = (
    ("Users",       "users",          "user_list",                  10, ["User Admins"]),
    ("Employees",   "user-round",     "employee_list",              20, ["User Admins", "HR"]),
    ("Leave",       "calendar-check", "leave_list",                 25, ["User Admins", "HR", "All Employees"]),
    ("Roster",      "calendar-days",  "roster_week",                30, ["User Admins", "Roster Planner"]),
    # Documents + Offboarding are section headers (blank URL) so the sidebar
    # template renders them as expandable sections whose submenus show below.
    # Giving them a URL would make them direct links and suppress submenus —
    # see templates/partials/sidebar.html.
    ("Documents",   "file-text",      "",                            35,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership", "All Employees"]),
    ("Offboarding", "door-open",      "",                            40,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership", "Line Managers",
         "Department Heads", "IT", "Finance", "Admin Facilities", "HR Head"]),
)

# Each entry: ``(main_title, sub_title, route_name, rank, [group_names])``.
# ``main_title`` must match an entry in ``ORBIS_MAIN_MENUS``; if the parent
# main menu is missing the row is skipped with a warning.
ORBIS_SUB_MENUS = (
    # Documents
    ("Documents", "Dashboard",         "documents:dashboard",            5,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership", "All Employees"]),
    ("Documents", "My documents",      "documents:my_documents",        10,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership", "All Employees"]),
    ("Documents", "Request document",  "documents:request_start",       20,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership", "All Employees"]),
    ("Documents", "Pending queue",     "documents:all_pending_queue",   30,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership"]),
    ("Documents", "All documents",     "documents:all_documents",       40,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership"]),
    # Offboarding
    ("Offboarding", "Create case (HR)", "offboarding:hr_create_resignation", 5,
        ["User Admins", "HR"]),
    ("Offboarding", "My offboarding",  "offboarding:my_offboarding",    10,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership", "All Employees"]),
    ("Offboarding", "Pending acks",    "offboarding:manager_ack_queue", 20,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Line Managers", "Department Heads"]),
    ("Offboarding", "Clearance queue", "offboarding:clearance_queue",   30,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "IT", "Finance", "Admin Facilities", "HR Head"]),
    ("Offboarding", "All cases",       "offboarding:case_list",         40,
        ["User Admins", "HR", "Senior Leadership"]),
)

# Canonical office codes (see accounts/locations.py).
CANONICAL_OFFICE_CODES = ("MBD", "MHK", "RAOWA")


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Seed Orbis groups, menus, locations, shifts, leave policies, and taxonomy."

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument(
            "--dry-run", action="store_true",
            help="Print the steps without writing anything (rolls back the transaction).",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--skip-taxonomy", action="store_true",
            help="Skip the Country/Division/State/City fixture (faster on re-runs).",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--skip-holidays", action="store_true",
            help="Skip the 2026 holidays fixture.",
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **opts):
        dry_run = opts["dry_run"]
        skip_taxonomy = opts["skip_taxonomy"]
        skip_holidays = opts["skip_holidays"]

        try:
            with transaction.atomic():
                self._seed_groups()
                self._loaddata("seed_org")
                self._seed_canonical_joblocations()
                if skip_taxonomy:
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING("[skip] employees taxonomy"))
                else:
                    self._loaddata("seed_taxonomy")
                self._call("seed_shifts")
                self._call("seed_leave_policies")
                self._call("seed_document_types")
                self._call("seed_offboarding_workflow")
                self._seed_main_menus()
                self._seed_submenus()
                self._call("sync_protected_views")
                if skip_holidays:
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING("[skip] 2026 holidays"))
                else:
                    self._loaddata("seed_holidays_2026")

                if dry_run:
                    self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING("[dry-run] rolling back"))
                    raise _DryRun()
        except _DryRun:
            return

        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS("✅ seed_orbis complete"))

    # ----- step helpers ---------------------------------------------------

    def _seed_groups(self):
        created = 0
        for name in ORBIS_GROUPS:
            _, made = Group.objects.get_or_create(name=name)
            created += int(made)
        self.stdout.write(f"groups: {len(ORBIS_GROUPS)} ensured ({created} new)")

    def _seed_canonical_joblocations(self):
        from accounts.locations import get_canonical_office_jobloc

        for code in CANONICAL_OFFICE_CODES:
            jl = get_canonical_office_jobloc(code)
            self.stdout.write(f"jobloc: {code} → {jl}")

    def _seed_main_menus(self):
        from dynamic_menu.models import MainMenu

        for title, icon, url, rank, group_names in ORBIS_MAIN_MENUS:
            mm, _ = MainMenu.objects.update_or_create(
                title=title,
                defaults={
                    "icon_class": icon,
                    "url": url,
                    "rank": rank,
                    "is_active": True,
                },
            )
            groups = list(Group.objects.filter(name__in=group_names))
            mm.groups.set(groups)
            self.stdout.write(
                f"menu: {title} (rank {rank}) → {[g.name for g in groups]}"
            )

    def _seed_submenus(self):
        from dynamic_menu.models import MainMenu, SubMenu

        if not ORBIS_SUB_MENUS:
            self.stdout.write("submenus: (none defined yet)")
            return

        for main_title, sub_title, url, rank, group_names in ORBIS_SUB_MENUS:
            try:
                main = MainMenu.objects.get(title=main_title)
            except MainMenu.DoesNotExist:
                self.stdout.write(self.style.WARNING(
                    f"submenu skip: parent menu '{main_title}' not found"
                ))
                continue
            sm, _ = SubMenu.objects.update_or_create(
                main_menu=main,
                title=sub_title,
                defaults={
                    "url": url,
                    "rank": rank,
                    "is_active": True,
                },
            )
            groups = list(Group.objects.filter(name__in=group_names))
            sm.groups.set(groups)
            self.stdout.write(
                f"submenu: {main_title} → {sub_title} (rank {rank}) → "
                f"{[g.name for g in groups]}"
            )

    # ----- thin wrappers --------------------------------------------------

    def _loaddata(self, fixture: str):
        self.stdout.write(f"loaddata: {fixture}")
        call_command("loaddata", fixture, verbosity=0)

    def _call(self, command: str, *args, **kwargs):
        self.stdout.write(f"call: {command}")
        call_command(command, *args, verbosity=0, **kwargs)


class _DryRun(Exception):
    """Sentinel: rolls back the outer atomic block on --dry-run."""
